107.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: AHD includes a CD4 count below 200 cells/mm³, and PEP is required within 72 hours of exposure. Infants require virological testing at birth or 6 weeks, not antibody testing at 28 days.

107.s: Which of the following is listed by WHO as an HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis option?
107.x: Long-acting injectable lenacapavir is one of the WHO PrEP options. Bone-marrow transplantation concerns the handful of documented cures, Mission Sampark concerns people lost to follow-up on ART, and dual HIV-syphilis kits are used for antenatal screening.
107.tq: Direct Recall · tests the “WHO PrEP options” angle

1. Under the YSRCP government during 2019–24, primary schools retained Classes 1–2, while Classes 3–5 were merged with nearby high schools.
2. Under the current NDA–TDP government, Model Primary Schools were envisaged at one per panchayat for Classes 3–5, while other schools were downgraded to Classes 1–2.
3. Both rounds of restructuring were not aligned with NEP 2020.
4.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct, so exactly two statements are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because both rounds followed NEP 2020-aligned restructuring.
4.tq: Multi-Statement Correctness · tests the “School restructuring models” angle
n: Government: YSRCP (2019–24); Model: School Rationalisation Policy (2023) — primary schools kept only Classes 1–2; Classes 3–5 merged with nearby high schools [November 2025 · School mergers in Andhra Pradesh]
Government: NDA–TDP (current); Model: Model Primary Schools (one per panchayat) for Classes 3–5; other schools downgraded to Classes 1–2 [November 2025 · School mergers in Andhra Pradesh]
Framework: both followed NEP 2020-aligned restructuring [November 2025 · School mergers in Andhra Pradesh]

29.s:

Targeted advertisements to children are restricted.

1. GST rates were changed for 546 goods, with over 80% witnessing cuts and around 20% witnessing increases.
2. The shift from 28% to 40% for some goods represented a real increase in the tax burden in every case.
3. Exempt goods do not provide Input Tax Credit.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
36.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The 28% to 40% movement for some goods reflected the merger of compensation cess and was not a real hike in every case.
36.tq: Multi-Statement Correctness · tests the “Revenue and tax-rate implications” angle
n: 546 goods changed — over 80% cuts, ~20% increases [September 2025 · 56th GST Council — two-tier GST of 5% and 18% (GST 2.0)]
⚠ 28% → 40% for some goods reflects merger of compensation cess, not a real hike [September 2025 · 56th GST Council — two-tier GST of 5% and 18% (GST 2.0)]
⚠ Exempt goods get no Input Tax Credit [September 2025 · 56th GST Council — two-tier GST of 5% and 18% (GST 2.0)]

36.s: In the context of the Supreme Court’s directions concerning DISCOMs, what is a regulatory asset?
o: A compulsory reserve created when ARR exceeds ACS and immediately refunded without interest
A gap arising when ACS exceeds ARR and deferred for later recovery with interest
A subsidy paid by the Ministry of Heavy Industries for EV charging stations
A battery-storage tender covering 1.7 GW across coal plants
36.x: A regulatory asset is the gap that arises when Average Cost of Supply exceeds Annual Revenue Requirement and is deferred for later recovery with interest. The other options describe EV infrastructure or battery-storage matters, or reverse the ACS–ARR relationship.
36.tq: Direct Recall · tests the “Definition of regulatory asset” angle
n: Regulatory asset: gap when Average Cost of Supply (ACS) > ARR, deferred for later recovery with interest [September 2025 · SC directions to DISCOMs on regulatory assets]

n: DISCOM: Punjab (2003-04); Regulatory assets: ₹487 crore — ⚠ first documented case [September 2025 · SC directions to DISCOMs on regulatory assets]

36.s: Which description best characterises India's position in the global dairy sector?
o: The world's largest milk producer, based on a government-owned dairy model
The world's largest milk producer, based on large-scale, pasture-based dairies
The world's second-largest milk producer, based on a smallholder, cooperative-led model
The world's largest milk producer, based on a smallholder, cooperative-led model

5.s: NTR Vaidya Seva is administered through which organisation and is primarily intended for which beneficiaries?

xs: **Dr NTR Vaidya Seva** is run by the **Dr NTR Vaidya Seva Trust** and gives cashless care to **BPL families** — option **(1)** is correct.
**SERP** delivers pensions; **NCCF** runs **Mee Mart** with Civil Supplies; **CDSCO** runs **SHRESTH**.

5.s: Which of the following correctly describes Sanjeevani?
o: A PDS-modernisation programme first introduced at Lalupuram
A digital health-profile and ABHA-ID programme, statewide from 1 January 2027 after a Kuppam pilot
A free-bus-travel programme for women, statewide from 15 August 2025
A poverty-eradication programme launched on Ugadi 2025

5.s: Under the hybrid NTR Vaidya Seva model announced in January 2025, trust-funded treatment for poor families is available up to:
5.x: The hybrid model provides insurance of ₹2.5 lakh per person for all residents and trust-funded treatment up to ₹25 lakh per family for poor families.

xs: Under the hybrid model (**Jan 2025**), Trust-funded treatment for the poor goes up to **₹25 lakh per family** (**APPSC 2025 key**) — option **(3)** is correct.
**₹2.5 lakh per person** is the **insurance layer** for all residents under the **Universal Health Policy**.
**₹5 lakh** is the per-family yearly procedure limit.
xa: ⚠ **₹2.5 lakh** = per person (insurance); **₹25 lakh** = per family (Trust); **₹5 lakh** = per family a year.

5.s:

Statement 2 is correct: total up to **₹25 lakh**.
Statements 3 and 4 are correct: **no limit for cancer**, and income eligibility up to **₹5 lakh** — so **1, 2, 3 and 4**, option **(4)**.

**PM-KISAN** is the farmer support folded into **Annadata Sukhibhava**, not a health scheme.
xa: AP Trust treatment for the poor: up to **₹25 lakh** per family.
Procedures: up to **₹5 lakh per family/yr**; **no limit for cancer**.
Eligibility: annual family income up to **₹5 lakh**.

State Housing and Rural Employment Support Technology Hub
Statewide Hospital Response and Emergency Treatment Helpline

**NCCF** works with Civil Supplies on **Mee Mart**; **SERP** delivers pensions; **Rythu Sadhikara Samstha** implements **APCNF**.

Trust treatment up to **₹25 lakh** per family; **no limit for cancer**.

5.s:
With reference to Thalliki Vandanam, consider the following statements:

3. It covers school-going children from Classes 1 to 12 from 2025–26.

xs: Statement 1 is correct: **₹15,000 per child per year**.
Statement 2 is correct: credited to the **mother**.
Statement 3 is correct: **every school-going child, Class 1 to 12**, from **2025-26** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: It was **Amma Vodi** (**Jan 2020**); covers **government or private schools**.

5.s: The cash assistance under Thalliki Vandanam is subject to which of the following conditions?
o: Enrolment only in a government school

xs: **Thalliki Vandanam** is a **conditional cash transfer** with **75% attendance** — option **(2)** is correct.

xa: Aim: lower **dropout** + higher **GER** (**G2-GS 2025 key**).

5.s:

2. Increase in the Gross Enrolment Ratio
3. Provision of pensions to mothers

100 per cent literacy drive of the Adult Education Department

5.s:

5.tq: Compare amount and unit of measurement before accepting a similarity statement.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: Telangana's **Rythu Bharosa** = **₹12,000 an acre**.
Statement 2 is correct: AP's **Annadata Sukhibhava** = **₹20,000 per farmer**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the unit (per acre vs per farmer) and amount differ — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: Annadata Sukhibhava includes **PM-KISAN's ₹6,000**; State share **₹14,000**.
Paid in **three instalments**.
AP's old **YSR Rythu Bharosa** is now **Annadata Sukhibhava**.

12.s:
With reference to the Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026-27, consider the following statements:

3. Capital expenditure increased by 47% over the previous year.

12.tq: Check the numerical statements together, especially the repeated percentage and rounded amount.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: revenue expenditure is **₹2,56,143 crore** (also given as **₹2,56,142 crore**) ≈ **₹2.56 lakh crore**.
Statement 2 is correct: capital outlay **₹48,698 crore** (also given as **₹48,697 crore**).
Statement 3 is correct: capital outlay rose **+47%** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: **RE 2025-26** capital outlay was **₹39,498 crore**.
⚠ Capital outlay **+47%**; total expenditure **+12%**.
Interest payments: **₹37,281 crore**.

12.s: The revenue deficit estimated in the Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026-27 was:

**₹37,281 crore** is **interest payments**; **₹75,868 crore (3.84%)** is the **fiscal deficit**.

12.s:

xs: Statement 1 is correct: RD fell from **2.33%** (2025-26 RE) to **1.11%**.

Exam angle: outlay **₹3.32 lakh crore** and ratios **RD 1.11%**, **FD 3.84%**.

xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Jyothi Yarraji** won **gold** at the **2022 National Games (Gujarat)** (PYQ).

Statement 3 is wrong: her **Arjuna 2024** was for **athletics**, not weightlifting — so option **(2) 1 and 2 only** is correct.

24.s: The SKOCH Award 2025 received by APCO was for which activity?
24.x: APCO received the SKOCH Award 2025 for handloom digitisation.
24.tq: Link the organisation with the exact award-winning activity.
xs: **APCO** won the **SKOCH Award 2025** for **handloom digitisation** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Tourism promotion** is the **GTM** recognition; **Basic Infrastructure** is **ASR** district's ADP rank; water conservation awards went to **Prakasam** villages.
xa: AP won **10 ODOP awards** (**4** handloom).
ODOP is run by **DPIIT** with the States.

24.s: Which institution from Andhra Pradesh was ranked first under the Department of Telecommunications initiative titled '100 5G Use Case Labs'?
24.x: IIITDM Kurnool was ranked first under the DoT initiative for 100 5G Use Case Labs during January–June 2026.
24.tq: Match the initiative with the institution rather than with a similarly named State body.
xs: **IIITDM Kurnool** ranked **1st** in DoT's **'100 5G Use Case Labs'** (Jan-Jun 2026) — option **(3)** is correct.
**APCO** won a **SKOCH** award; **DPRC Chittoor** the capacity-building award; **APFDC** is reviving the Nandi Awards.
xa: **ASR** district was **1st in India** in **Basic Infrastructure** under NITI Aayog's ADP.
GTM named AP **"Best Tourism Promotion State"**.

24.s: Kuppam in Chittoor district entered the Guinness record for distributing how many e-cycles in one day?
24.x: Kuppam set a Guinness record by distributing 5,555 e-cycles in one day.
24.tq: Retain the exact repeated-digit figure in a numerical current-affairs fact.
xs: **Kuppam** (Chittoor) set a **Guinness record** by distributing **5,555 e-cycles** in one day (**1 Feb 2026**) — option **(2)** is correct.
**Kuppam** is a mandal of **Chittoor** district.
xa: ⚠ AP's other Guinness record: **largest Dhimsa dance**, **Bhogapuram**, **31 Jul 2026**.
**Kuppam** mandal was **3rd** in the Nanaji Deshmukh Sarvottam Panchayat Satat Vikas Puraskar 2025.

24.s: Which State-level recognition was associated with GTM?
24.x: GTM recognised Andhra Pradesh as the Best Tourism Promotion State.
24.tq: Match the award title with the sector in which it was conferred.
xs: **GTM** named AP the **"Best Tourism Promotion State"** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Panchayat capacity building** was won by **Chittoor's DPRC**; **handloom digitisation** by **APCO** (SKOCH); **Basic Infrastructure** by **ASR** district.
xa: AP also won **10 ODOP awards** (**4** handloom).
The **Panchayat Raj Dept** won a national award for the **2nd** straight year.

24.s: In NITI Aayog's Aspirational Districts Programme ranking (March 2026), which Andhra Pradesh district was 1st in India, and in which theme?
o: Alluri Sitharama Raju — Health and Nutrition
24.x: Alluri Sitharama Raju (ASR) district ranked 1st in India in Basic Infrastructure under the ADP (Mar 2026). Chittoor's 1st place was for its District Panchayat Resource Centre (capacity building), and Prakasam's villages won water awards, not an ADP rank. Health and Nutrition is the wrong theme.
24.tq: ADP Mar 2026: ASR district — No. 1, Basic Infrastructure.
xs: **Alluri Sitharama Raju (ASR)** district ranked **1st in India** in **Basic Infrastructure** in NITI Aayog's ADP (Mar 2026) — option **(1)** is correct.
**Chittoor's** 1st place was for its **District Panchayat Resource Centre**; **Prakasam's** villages won **water** awards, not an ADP rank.
xa: **Murugummi** (Prakasam) was **2nd-best Village Panchayat** (6th National Water Awards 2024).
**IIITDM Kurnool** was **1st** in DoT's '100 5G Use Case Labs'.

24.s: The Asian Games scheduled in Aichi-Nagoya from September 2026 include which Andhra Pradesh-related athletes in the squad?
o: Srimushnam V. Raja Rao and D. Sivamma
24.x: Jyothi Yarraji and Satwik were mentioned as members of the squad for the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games.
24.tq: Match the current sporting event with the athletes specifically associated with it.
xs: **Jyothi Yarraji** and **Satwik** are in the squad for the **Aichi-Nagoya** Asian Games (from **Sep 2026**) — option **(3)** is correct.

**Deepika Reddy** and **Neelabonu Satyam** are artists; **Srimushnam V. Raja Rao** got a music title and **D. Sivamma** is a puppeteer; **Malleswari** and **Ajaya Babu** are weightlifters not named in the squad.
xa: Satwik and Chirag Shetty are **defending Asian Games champions**.
**Ajaya Babu's** CWG silver came in **Jul 2026**.
Some notes (**11 Sep 2026**) say AP's sports system has "run dry".

24.s:
Consider the following statements about sports infrastructure and recruitment in Andhra Pradesh:
1. The State was criticised for having few AstroTurfs.
2. Vizag was reported to lack a synthetic track.
3. Disputes existed over recruitment through the sports quota.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
24.x: All three statements reflect the reported criticism of sports infrastructure and sports-quota recruitment in Andhra Pradesh.
24.tq: Group related criticisms and verify whether the option captures all the stated issues.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Critics cite **few AstroTurfs** and **no synthetic track in Vizag**.
There are also **disputes over sports-quota recruitment**.
xa: AP's only three hockey AstroTurfs: **Kakinada, Kadapa, Pulivendula**.
The sports quota in **Mega DSC-2025** was debated (Aug-Sep 2026).
Coaches say AP lost its sports infrastructure to **Hyderabad** in **2014**.

24.s:
With reference to Padma awards and Article 18 of the Constitution, consider the following statements:
1. Padma awards are not titles under Article 18.
2. Padma awards cannot be used as a prefix or suffix.
3. The position was affirmed in Balaji Raghavan (1996).
Which of the statements given above are correct?
24.x: All three statements are correct. Balaji Raghavan (1996) held that Padma awards are not titles under Article 18 and cannot be used as prefixes or suffixes.
24.tq: Combine the constitutional principle, consequence and judicial authority before selecting the code.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Padma awards** are not "titles" under **Art. 18**, so they **cannot be used as prefix/suffix**.
This was held in **Balaji Raghavan** (**1996**).
xa: The **Padma Awards 2026** totalled **131** (**5** Vibhushan, **13** Bhushan, **113** Shri).
**Four** people from AP received Padma awards in **2026**.

24.s: Which statement best captures the infrastructure-related criticism concerning Andhra Pradesh sports after 2014?
o: Andhra Pradesh transferred all its sports infrastructure to Visakhapatnam after 2014.
Coaches stated that Hyderabad lost its sports infrastructure to Andhra Pradesh in 2014, while the SAAP centre at ANU expanded.
Coaches stated that Andhra Pradesh lost its sports infrastructure to Hyderabad in 2014, and the SAAP centre at ANU was later closed.
The SAAP centre at ANU was converted into the State’s principal airport.
24.x: Coaches said Andhra Pradesh lost sports infrastructure to Hyderabad in 2014 and that the SAAP centre at ANU, which trained Jyothi Yarraji, was later closed.
24.tq: Watch for reversed comparisons and altered institutional actions in a long statement.
xs: Coaches say **AP lost its sports infrastructure to Hyderabad** in **2014**, and the **SAAP centre at ANU** was later **closed** — option **(3)** is correct.
Option (2) reverses the direction of the loss; options (1) and (4) are not in the notes.
xa: The closed ANU centre had trained **Jyothi Yarraji**.
Critics also cite **no synthetic track in Vizag** and few AstroTurfs.

24.s: Which city in Andhra Pradesh hosts most of the major events such as IFR, MILAN, NCeG and BRICS?
24.x: Visakhapatnam hosts most of the major events listed, including IFR, MILAN, NCeG and BRICS.
24.tq: Match the concentration of major events with the correct host city.
xs: **Visakhapatnam** hosts most big events — **IFR**, **MILAN**, **NCeG** and **BRICS** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Tirupati** hosted the Thyagaraja festival and Amaravati Championship; **Vijayawada** the Avakaya Festival; **Rajamahendravaram** will host the largest Pushkaram tent city.
xa: **IFR 2026** (the 3rd): **18 Feb 2026**, **71 warships**, theme **"United through Oceans"**.
**BRICS** sports meet: **22-23 Aug 2026** — **BRICS Sports Joint Declaration**.
**NCeG** (28th, Sep 2025) produced the **Visakhapatnam Declaration**.

31.s:
Consider the following statements about the Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026:
1. It replaces the Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021.
2. It sets up a National Tribunals Commission headquartered in Mumbai.
3. The Commission has five members, with a tenure of five years or up to age 70.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
31.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Bill replaces the 2021 Act. Statement 2 is wrong: the Commission's headquarters is New Delhi. Statement 3 is correct: five members; five-year tenure or age 70. So B; A, C and D include the false statement 2.
31.tq: National Tribunals Commission = New Delhi, 5 members, 5 years/70.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the **Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026** replaces the **2021 Act**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the **National Tribunals Commission** is headquartered in **New Delhi**, not Mumbai.
Statement 3 is correct: **5 members**, **5-year tenure or age 70** — so option **(2) 1 and 3 only** is correct.
xa: The Bill was introduced in the **Lok Sabha** in Aug 2026.
**Madras Bar Association v. UoI** (2025) struck down parts of the **Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021**.

31.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Kerala (Alteration of Name) Act, 2026:
1. It changes the name of Kerala to Keralam.
2. The change was approved by the Lok Sabha on 11 August 2026 and by the Rajya Sabha on 12 August 2026.
3. The name of the High Court is also changed by the Act.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
31.x: The Act changes Kerala to Keralam, with Lok Sabha approval on 11 August and Rajya Sabha approval on 12 August 2026. The High Court name remains unchanged.
31.tq: Find the false statement by checking the exception relating to the High Court.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Act renames **Kerala → "Keralam"**; **LS 11 Aug**, **RS 12 Aug 2026** — option **(1) 1 and 2 only** is correct.
Statement 3 is wrong: the **High Court name is unchanged**.
xa: The change is made in the **First Schedule** under **Art. 3**; assent and notification came in Aug 2026.
Another renaming in news: **Nauru** → Republic of **Naoero** (Aug 2026).
AP's **Jonnagiri Gold Mine** became **Swarnagiri Gold Mine** (CDCA Jul 2026).

31.s: The Kerala (Alteration of Name) Act, 2026, operates through an alteration in which constitutional provision and Schedule?
31.x: The change from Kerala to Keralam is made under Article 3 and involves the First Schedule of the Constitution.
31.tq: Apply the article-and-Schedule pairing technique used for constitutional amendments.
xs: The **Kerala → Keralam** change works through **Art. 3** and the **First Schedule** — option **(3) Article 3 and the First Schedule** is correct.
It was passed by Parliament (**LS 11 Aug**, **RS 12 Aug 2026**) as an ordinary law, not an **Art. 368** amendment.
xa: The **High Court** keeps its old name.
AP now has **28 districts** (since **Dec 2025**; **26** from **Apr 2022**).

31.s:
Consider the following statements about the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment, 2026:
1. It provides 5-10 years' jail and a fine of up to Rs 50 lakh.
2. The probe must be completed within 90 days.
3. It provides for special fast-track courts.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
31.x: Statement 1 is correct: 5-10 years' jail and a fine up to Rs 50 lakh. Statement 2 is wrong: the probe must finish within 60 days. Statement 3 is correct: special fast-track courts are provided. So B; A, C and D include the false statement 2.
31.tq: Paper-leak law 2026: 5-10 yrs, Rs 50 lakh, 60-day probe, fast-track courts.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **5-10 years' jail** and a fine up to **₹50 lakh**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the probe must finish within **60 days**, not 90.
Statement 3 is correct: **special fast-track courts** — so option **(2) 1 and 3 only** is correct.
xa: It amends the **2024 Act**; assent on **31 Jul 2026**; probes by **STFs**.
It followed **Gen-Z student protests** over paper leaks and the Education Minister's resignation (**25 Jul 2026**).

31.s: The Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025, is associated with which of the following provisions?
o: Regulation of only educational online games
A ban on real-money games and establishment of an Online Gaming Authority of India under the 2026 Rules
Transfer of online gaming regulation exclusively to State Governments
A ban on all forms of online games, including recreational games
31.x: The Act bans real-money games, while the 2026 Rules establish the Online Gaming Authority of India from 1 May 2026.
31.tq: Distinguish a targeted prohibition from an exaggerated ban on every online game.
xs: The **Online Gaming Act, 2025** **bans real-money games**, and its **Rules 2026** set up the **Online Gaming Authority of India** — option **(2)** is correct.
The Authority functions from **1 May 2026**; recreational games are not banned outright, so option (4) is wrong.
xa: Other 2025 Acts: **SHANTI Act** (nuclear) and **VB-G RAM G Act** (replaces MGNREGA).
The **DPDP Rules 2025** complete the data-protection regime under the DPDP Act 2023.

31.s:
Consider the following statements about the SHANTI Act, 2025:
1. It replaced the Atomic Energy Act, 1962 and the Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act, 2010.
2. It imposes unlimited supplier liability for nuclear damage.
3. It caps liability at 300 million SDR.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
31.x: Statement 1 is correct: it replaced the 1962 Act and CLNDA 2010. Statement 2 is wrong: the Act has no supplier liability. Statement 3 is correct: the cap is 300 million SDR. So B; A, C and D include the false statement 2.
31.tq: SHANTI = no supplier liability, limited private role, 300 mn SDR cap.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **SHANTI** replaced the **Atomic Energy Act 1962** and **CLNDA 2010**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the Act has **no supplier liability**.
Statement 3 is correct: the cap is **300 mn SDR** — so option **(2) 1 and 3 only** is correct.
xa: It allows a **limited private role**; draft Rules came in 2026.
⚠ **SHANTI** replaced two laws (**1962** + **2010**); **VB-G RAM G** replaced **MGNREGA**.

31.s: The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment, 2026, increased the sanctioned strength of the Supreme Court from 34 to:
31.x: The amendment increases the Supreme Court strength from 34 to 38, comprising 37 judges apart from the Chief Justice of India.
31.tq: Distinguish the total strength from the number of judges excluding the CJI.
xs: The **Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment, 2026** raised the strength from **34 → 38** (**37 + CJI**) — option **(4) 38 judges** is correct.
It amends the **1956 Act** (Art. 124) and was passed as a **Money Bill** (Aug 2026).
xa: It replaced a **May 2026** ordinance under **Art. 123**; the Bill passed the LS on **3 Aug 2026**.
CJI: **Surya Kant**; SC pendency ~**88,000** cases (**2025**).

31.s: The Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment), 2026, makes insulting or disrupting which of the following punishable?
31.x: The amendment to the 1971 Act makes insulting or disrupting Vande Mataram punishable.
31.tq: Use the exact protected national symbol instead of substituting a more familiar one.
xs: The **Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment), 2026** makes insulting or disrupting **Vande Mataram** punishable — option **(4)** is correct.
It amends the **1971 Act**.
xa: The Act being amended dates from **1971**; the 2026 change adds **Vande Mataram** to its protection.
Other 2026 amendments: **Transgender Persons** (removes self-determination of gender) and **MMDR** (critical minerals).

31.s: The MMDR Amendment, 2026, is primarily concerned with which subject and ministry?
o: Critical minerals fiscal regime — Ministry of Mines
Coal mine rehabilitation — Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Rare earth research — Ministry of Science and Technology
31.x: The MMDR Amendment, 2026, establishes a fiscal regime for critical minerals and is associated with the Ministry of Mines.
31.tq: Match the legislative subject with the responsible ministry.
xs: The **MMDR Amendment, 2026** sets a **critical minerals fiscal regime** under the **Ministry of Mines** — option **(1)** is correct.
The notes link it to no other ministry; coal rehabilitation, petroleum tax and rare-earth research are not its subject.
xa: Other 2026 laws: **Registration of Births and Deaths (Amdt)**, **MSME Development (Amdt)**, **NCDC (Amdt)** and an **IBC** amendment.
The **Taxation and Other Laws (Amdt)** replaced an Income-tax Ordinance.

31.s: Which one of the following amendments removes self-determination of gender?
31.x: The Transgender Persons (Amendment), 2026, removes self-determination of gender; the amendment was made in March 2026.
31.tq: Apply the provision to the legislation most directly connected with the subject.
xs: The **Transgender Persons (Amendment), 2026** **removes self-determination of gender** (Mar 2026) — option **(4)** is correct.
The other three amendments do not appear in the notes' list of 2026 laws.
xa: Other 2026 laws: **unified CAPF personnel law**; **Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amdt)** on **Vande Mataram**.
**Public Examinations Amendment, 2026**: assent **31 Jul 2026**.

31.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026:
1. It replaced a May 2026 ordinance.
2. It was passed as a Money Bill.
3. The Rajya Sabha rejected it outright.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
31.x: The Bill replaced the May 2026 ordinance and was passed as a Money Bill. The Rajya Sabha only returned it; it did not reject it outright.
31.tq: Distinguish ‘returned’ from ‘rejected’ when testing the role of the second House.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the Bill replaced the **May 2026 ordinance** (**Art. 123**).
Statement 2 is correct: it was **passed as a Money Bill** (Aug 2026).
Statement 3 is wrong: the Bill was **passed**, not rejected — so option **(1) 1 and 2 only** is correct.
xa: Strength: **34 → 38** (**37** judges + CJI); amends the **1956 Act** (Art. 124).
The LS passed it on **3 Aug 2026**.
⚠ **Art. 123** = President's ordinance; **Art. 213** = Governor's ordinance.

31.s: Under the VB-G RAM G Act, 2025, the proposed number of days of employment is:
31.x: The VB-G RAM G Act, 2025 is stated to replace MGNREGA and provide 125 days of employment.
31.tq: Test the precise employment-days figure in the current policy provision.
xs: The **VB-G RAM G Act, 2025** provides **125 days** of employment — option **(3)** is correct.
It **replaces MGNREGA** from **1 Jul 2026**.
xa: Its **base wage** is **₹300/day**.
⚠ **VB-G RAM G** replaced **MGNREGA**; **SHANTI** replaced **1962** + **2010** nuclear laws.

31.s: The Constitution (Jammu and Kashmir) Scheduled Tribes Order (Amendment) Bill, 2024, passed by the Rajya Sabha on 9 February 2024, amended which of the following?
o: Constitution (Jammu and Kashmir) Scheduled Tribes Order, 1989
Constitution (Jammu and Kashmir) Scheduled Castes Order, 1956
31.x: The 2024 Bill amended the Constitution (J&K) Scheduled Tribes Order, 1989 (PYQ). The 1950 Order is the general ST Order for other States, the SC Order deals with Scheduled Castes, and the Reorganisation Order is not an ST list.
31.tq: J&K ST Order Amendment Bill 2024 → amends the 1989 Order.
xs: The **2024 Bill** (RS, **9 Feb 2024**) amended the **Constitution (J&K) Scheduled Tribes Order, 1989** — option **(1)** is correct (PYQ).
The notes link the Bill only to the **1989** J&K ST Order, not to the 1950, 1956 or 2019 orders.
xa: Other asked-before item: **IBC 2016** got assent in **May 2016**; **IBBI** has **10** members.
**Art. 371-K** was proposed for **Ladakh** (**Sep 2026**).

31.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 received Presidential assent in December 2016.
2. The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) has 7 members.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
31.x: Both are wrong: the IBC received assent in May 2016, and the IBBI has 10 members. So D; A, B and C each accept at least one false statement. This mirrors a question asked before in which both statements were wrong.
31.tq: IBC assent May 2016; IBBI = 10 members.
xs: Both statements are wrong — option **(4) Neither 1 nor 2** is correct.
**IBC 2016** got assent in **May 2016**, not December.
**IBBI** has **10** members, not 7.
xa: ⚠ This was **asked before**, and both statements were wrong in that question too.
An **IBC amendment** was among the 2026 laws.

31.s: The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Ordinance, 2026, was promulgated under which Article of the Constitution?
31.x: The Ordinance was promulgated by the President under Article 123 in May 2026. Article 124 relates to the Supreme Court itself and its judges.
31.tq: Distinguish the ordinance-making Article from the substantive constitutional provision.
xs: The **SC (Number of Judges) Amendment Ordinance, 2026** was promulgated under **Art. 123** (**Article 123**) — option **(1)** is correct.
**Art. 213** is the **Governor's** ordinance power; **Art. 124** is in the 1956 judges law; **Art. 368** is constitutional amendment.
xa: The ordinance (May) raised the strength **33 → 37** judges + CJI (**34 → 38** incl. CJI).
It was replaced by a Bill passed by the LS on **3 Aug 2026**.

31.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. AP Human Organ Transplantation Ordinance — June 2026
2. Sri City University Ordinance — Article 213
3. Supreme Court Number of Judges Ordinance — Article 213
Which of the statements given above are correct?
31.x: The AP Human Organ Transplantation Ordinance was promulgated in June 2026, and the Sri City University Ordinance was issued under Article 213. The Supreme Court Ordinance was promulgated under Article 123, not Article 213.
31.tq: Use the constitutional division between Union and State ordinance powers to detect the swapped Article.
xs: Pair 1 is correct: the **AP Human Organ Transplantation Ordinance** came in **Jun 2026**.
Pair 2 is correct: the **Sri City University** ordinance is under **Art. 213**.
Pair 3 is wrong: the **SC judges ordinance** was under **Art. 123** — so option **(1) 1 and 2 only** is correct.
xa: ⚠ **Art. 123** = President's ordinance; **Art. 213** = Governor's ordinance (State level).
The **Ordinance** route is itself a criticised trend in 2026.

31.s: The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026, replaced an ordinance that had increased the sanctioned strength of judges from:
o: 38 to 42, excluding the Chief Justice of India
34 to 38, including the Chief Justice of India
31.x: The Bill replaced the May 2026 ordinance and increased the number of judges from 34 to 38, including the CJI.
31.tq: Watch both the before-and-after figures and the inclusion of the CJI.
xs: The ordinance raised SC strength from **34 to 38, including the CJI** — option **(4)** is correct.
Counting judges other than the CJI, it is **33 → 37**.
xa: It was promulgated under **Art. 123** in **May 2026**; the replacing Bill passed the LS on **3 Aug 2026**.
The amending law changes the **1956 Act** (Art. 124).

31.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 — Indian Evidence Act, 1872
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 — Indian Penal Code, 1860
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 — Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 — Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973
31.x: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 replaced the Indian Penal Code, 1860. The Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 was replaced by the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
31.tq: Use the wrong-law replacement trap by separating the three criminal codes.
xs: **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023** replaced the **IPC, 1860**, not the CrPC — so pair **(4)** is NOT correctly matched.
The **CrPC, 1973** was replaced by the **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023**.
**Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023** replaced the **Indian Evidence Act, 1872**.
xa: The **Four Labour Codes** (in force **21 Nov 2025**) replaced **29** labour laws.
**Income Tax Act, 2025** replaced the **Income-tax Act, 1961**.

31.s: The four Labour Codes, which came into force on 21 November 2025, replaced how many labour laws?
31.x: The four Labour Codes came into force on 21 November 2025 and replaced 29 labour laws.
31.tq: Recall the exact replacement count and date-linked reform.
xs: The **Four Labour Codes** (in force **21 Nov 2025**) replaced **29** labour laws — option **(3)** is correct.
They came into force on **21 Nov 2025**.
xa: The **Industrial Relations Code** absorbed the **ID Act 1947** and the **Trade Unions Act 1926**.
A **9-judge** Bench (Aug 2026) held the **1978 Bangalore Water Supply** definition of "industry" does **not** apply to the **IRC, 2020**.

31.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Industrial Relations Code (IRC) in relation to the labour-law reforms?
o: It absorbed the Atomic Energy Act, 1962 and the CLNDA, 2010.
It replaced only the Income-tax Act, 1961.
It absorbed the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 and the Trade Unions Act, 1926.
It formed part of the DPDP Rules, 2025.
31.x: The Industrial Relations Code absorbed the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 and the Trade Unions Act, 1926.
31.tq: Match the specific code with the statutes absorbed by it.
xs: The **IRC** absorbed the **Industrial Disputes Act, 1947** and the **Trade Unions Act, 1926** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Atomic Energy Act 1962** and **CLNDA 2010** were replaced by the **SHANTI Act**; the **Income-tax Act, 1961** by the **Income Tax Act, 2025**.
xa: The Four Labour Codes replaced **29** laws, in force **21 Nov 2025**.
The SC's 9-judge Bench under **CJI Surya Kant** ruled on "industry" under the **IRC, 2020**.

31.s: The Income Tax Act, 2025 replaced which of the following laws?
31.x: The Income Tax Act, 2025 replaced the Income-tax Act, 1961 (it came into force on 1 Apr 2026). The 1922 Act had already been replaced by the 1961 Act; the Wealth-tax Act and a Finance Act are different laws.
31.tq: Income Tax Act 2025 ← Income-tax Act 1961.
xs: The **Income Tax Act, 2025** replaced the **Income-tax Act, 1961** — option **(1)** is correct.
The **Taxation and Other Laws (Amdt), 2026** replaced an Income-tax Ordinance.
xa: **RUPPs** get tax exemption under **s.12, Income Tax Act 2025**.
Other new laws: **BNS** (IPC), **BNSS** (CrPC), **BSA** (Evidence Act).

31.s:
Consider the following statements about the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026:
1. It proposed raising the Lok Sabha cap from 550 to 850.
2. It proposed using the 2021 Census to fast-track women's reservation.
3. It was defeated in the Lok Sabha because it fell short of the special majority under Article 368.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
31.x: Statement 1 is correct: the cap was to go from 550 to 850. Statement 2 is wrong: the Bill used the 2011 Census. Statement 3 is correct: the vote was 298-230 of 528 voting, short of the Art. 368 special majority. So B; A, C and D include the false statement 2.
31.tq: 131st = 550 to 850, 2011 Census, defeated 298-230 (Art. 368).
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the **131st Amendment Bill** proposed raising the LS cap **550 → 850**.
Statement 2 is wrong: it used the **2011 Census**, not 2021.
Statement 3 is correct: it was **defeated 298-230** of **528** voting, short of the **Art. 368** special majority — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
xa: Its aim was **women's quota by 2029**; the **Delimitation Bill 2026** was **withdrawn**.
The defeat (**Apr 2026**) is one of the year's biggest polity events.

31.s:
Consider the following statements about the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023:
1. It is also known as the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam.
2. It provides women's reservation through Article 334A.
3. The women's quota took effect at once, without waiting for the Census or delimitation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
31.x: Statement 1 is correct: the 106th Amendment is the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, 2023. Statement 2 is correct: the quota is in Art. 334A. Statement 3 is wrong: the quota starts only after the Census and delimitation. So A; B, C and D include the false statement 3.
31.tq: 106th = Nari Shakti Vandan, Art. 334A, starts after Census + delimitation.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the **106th Amendment** (2023) is the **Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam**.
Statement 2 is correct: the quota is in **Art. 334A**.
Statement 3 is wrong: it **starts after the Census and delimitation** (tied to **Census 2027**) — so option **(1) 1 and 2 only** is correct.
xa: The **131st Amendment Bill, 2026** tried to fast-track this quota but was **defeated**.
⚠ **129th** = ONOE (Art. 82A); **130th** = removal after **30** days' custody.

31.s: The Constitution (130th Amendment) Bill, 2025 proposed automatic removal from office of which persons after being held in custody for 30 consecutive days on serious charges?
o: Judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts
The Prime Minister, Chief Ministers and Ministers
31.x: The Bill proposed the automatic removal of the Prime Minister, Chief Ministers or Ministers if held in custody for 30 consecutive days for charges carrying a possible sentence of five years or more.
31.tq: Match the proposed power and its office-holders without expanding the provision to unrelated constitutional authorities.
xs: The **130th Amendment Bill, 2025** provides for removal of the **PM, CMs or Ministers** held in custody for **30 consecutive days** — option **(4)** is correct.
The charges must carry **5+ years'** jail.
xa: The Bill is with a **JPC** whose deadline was extended (Jul 2026).
It was left out of the **2026 Monsoon Session** agenda.

31.s: For the removal mechanism proposed in the Constitution (130th Amendment) Bill, 2025, the charges must carry a possible imprisonment of at least:
31.x: The proposed mechanism applied to charges carrying a sentence of five years or more, along with the 30-day custody condition.
31.tq: Separate the imprisonment threshold from the independent 30-day custody requirement.
xs: The charges must carry **5+ years'** imprisonment — option **(2) 5 years** is correct.
This is combined with custody for **30 consecutive days**.
xa: The Bill covers the **PM, CMs or Ministers**.
⚠ **106th** = women's quota (Art. 334A); **129th** = ONOE; **131st** = defeated.

31.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Constitution (130th Amendment) Bill, 2025 is correct?
o: It was defeated in the Lok Sabha by 298 votes to 230.
It was placed on the agenda of the July 2026 Monsoon Session and immediately enacted.
It amended Article 82A to introduce simultaneous elections.
It was left out of the July 2026 Monsoon Session agenda and was associated with a Joint Parliamentary Committee whose deadline was extended.
31.x: The Bill was left out of the July 2026 Monsoon Session agenda; it was before a Joint Parliamentary Committee and its deadline was extended. The other options describe the 131st or 129th proposals.
31.tq: Use the bill-number and status distinction to avoid swapping provisions among constitutional amendment proposals.
xs: The **130th Amendment Bill** was **left out of the 2026 Monsoon Session** agenda and is with a **JPC** whose deadline was extended — option **(4)** is correct.
The **298-230** defeat belongs to the **131st** Bill; **Art. 82A** (simultaneous elections) belongs to the **129th** Bill.
xa: The 130th Bill covers removal after **30 consecutive days** in custody on **5+ years'** charges.
Bills passed without debate amid **2026 Monsoon Session** deadlocks drew criticism.

31.s:
Consider the following statements about the Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024 on One Nation One Election:
1. It proposes a new Article 82A.
2. It amends Articles 330 and 332.
3. It is with a Joint Parliamentary Committee.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
31.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Bill inserts a new Art. 82A. Statement 2 is wrong: it amends Arts. 83 and 172, not Arts. 330 and 332. Statement 3 is correct: the Bill is with the JPC. So B; A, C and D include the false statement 2.
31.tq: ONOE = new 82A + amend 83 (Parliament's term) and 172 (Assembly's term).
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the **129th Bill (2024)** adds a new **Art. 82A**.
Statement 2 is wrong: it amends **Arts. 83 and 172**, not 330 and 332.
Statement 3 is correct: it is with the **JPC** — so option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
xa: **Chidambaram** called it unconstitutional (Aug 2026).
**Arts. 330 and 332** are among the delimitation/reservation Articles (with **82** and **170**).

31.s: The Punjab and Haryana High Court struck down which policy?
o: Bihar's 85% reservation in all Union Government jobs
Haryana's 75% reservation of private-sector jobs for local residents
A 50% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha
Assam's reservation for members of the Legislative Assembly
31.x: The Punjab and Haryana High Court struck down Haryana's policy reserving 75% of private-sector jobs for local residents.
31.tq: Identify the exact State, sector and percentage in a domicile-reservation dispute.
xs: The **Punjab & Haryana HC** struck down **Haryana's 75%** private-job reservation for locals (PYQ) — option **(2)** is correct.
**Bihar's 85%** was a **proposal** (2025) in the **50% ceiling** debate, not a struck-down policy.
xa: The Centre **opposes creamy layer for SC/ST** (**Aug 2026**).
AP fixed a **33.33% BC quota** in ULB polls (G.O. Rt. No. **1065**).

31.s: Which issue is associated with Bihar's proposed 85% reservation in 2025?
o: The electoral college for the Vice-President
The constitutional limit or ceiling of 50% on reservations
The number of Lok Sabha seats under Article 82A
31.x: Bihar's proposal for 85% reservation led to debate concerning the 50% reservation ceiling.
31.tq: Connect the numerical proposal with the constitutional issue it raises, rather than with unrelated reservation provisions.
xs: **Bihar's 85%** proposal (**2025**) is linked to the **50% ceiling** debate on reservations — option **(2)** is correct.
**85%** would far exceed the **50%** ceiling, which is why it sparked the debate.
xa: **Haryana's 75%** local private-job quota was struck down by the **Punjab & Haryana HC**.
AP: **33.33% BC quota in ULB polls** (**19 Aug 2026**).
The Centre **opposes a creamy layer** for SC/ST (**Aug 2026**).

31.s: The Assam Uniform Civil Code Bill, 2026 is significant because it is:
o: A Union law applicable only to Parliament
The second UCC Bill in the North-East and the fifth at the State level
The first UCC Bill in India and the first in the North-East
The first UCC Bill in the North-East and the third at the State level in India
31.x: The Assam UCC Bill, 2026 was described as the first such Bill in the North-East and the third State-level UCC Bill overall.
31.tq: Compare the regional and national ranking separately to avoid reversing first and third.
xs: The **Assam UCC Bill, 2026** is the **first in the North-East** and the **third State** overall — option **(4)** is correct.
It is a **State** Bill, not a Union law, so option (1) is wrong.
xa: **Art. 371-K** has been proposed for **Ladakh** (**Sep 2026**).
In Assam's 2026 polls, the **NDA** won **102** seats and **Himanta Biswa Sarma** began a 2nd term.

31.s:
Consider the following statements about Lok Sabha delimitation:
1. The Lok Sabha now has 543 seats.
2. The present seat allocation is frozen on the basis of the 2001 Census.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
31.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Lok Sabha has 543 seats. Statement 2 is wrong: the allocation is frozen on the 1971 Census (54.8 crore). So A; B and C wrongly accept statement 2, and D wrongly rejects statement 1.
31.tq: 543 seats frozen on 1971 Census; next readjustment after Census 2027.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the **Lok Sabha** has **543** seats.
Statement 2 is wrong: seats are frozen on the **1971 Census** (**54.8 crore**), not 2001 — so option **(1) 1 only** is correct.
xa: The next readjustment comes after **Census 2027**.

31.s: The next readjustment of seats is expected after the:
31.x: The next readjustment of seats is expected after Census 2027.
31.tq: Use the future Census reference as the decisive discriminator.
xs: The next readjustment of seats is due after **Census 2027** — option **(1)** is correct.
The present **543** seats are frozen on the **1971** Census.
xa: The **106th Amendment** women's quota is also tied to **Census 2027** + delimitation.
The defeated **131st** Bill wanted to use the **2011 Census**.

31.s: Which set of Articles is associated with delimitation and reservation of seats in the legislatures?
31.x: Articles 82, 170, 330 and 332 are the constitutional provisions identified in connection with delimitation and legislative reservations.
31.tq: Identify the complete constitutional-Article cluster instead of a single provision.
xs: Delimitation and reserved seats are linked to **Articles 82, 170, 330 and 332** — option **(1)** is correct.
The notes list exactly these four Articles under delimitation; **Art. 368** belongs to constitutional amendment.
xa: Delimitation orders are **not challengeable in court**.
The government plan raises seats ~**50%**; southern seats **129 → 195**.

31.s: Which statement regarding orders made by delimitation authorities is correct?
o: They lapse automatically after every general election.
They are routinely challengeable before every High Court.
They are not challengeable in court.
They can be challenged only by the Election Commission.
31.x: Orders relating to delimitation are not challengeable in court.
31.tq: Test the constitutional finality or judicial-review status of a delimitation order.
xs: Delimitation orders are **not challengeable in court** — option **(3)** is correct.
So they neither lapse after elections nor go routinely before High Courts.
xa: LS seats (**543**) are frozen on the **1971** Census; next readjustment after **Census 2027**.
Southern States worry about federal fairness and delimitation, along with the **16th FC**.

31.s:
Consider the following statements about the government's delimitation plan:
1. It uses an 816-seat formula for the Lok Sabha.
2. Seats rise by about 50% while the southern States' share is kept at 23.8%.
3. The southern States' seats rise from 129 to 159.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
31.x: Statement 1 is correct: the plan uses an 816-seat formula. Statement 2 is correct: seats up about 50% with the southern share kept at 23.8%. Statement 3 is wrong: southern seats go from 129 to 195. So A; B, C and D include the false statement 3.
31.tq: 816 seats; South 129 to 195; share 23.8% kept.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the plan uses an **816-seat formula**.
Statement 2 is correct: seats rise ~**50%** with the southern share kept at **23.8%**.
Statement 3 is wrong: southern seats rise **129 → 195**, not 159 — so option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
xa: Present LS strength: **543**, frozen on the **1971** Census (**54.8 crore**).
The defeated **131st** Bill proposed a cap of **850**.

31.s: Which position was associated with the Centre in August 2026 regarding reservation for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes?
o: It transferred the issue entirely to local bodies.
It supported a creamy layer within SC/ST reservations.
It proposed abolition of SC/ST reservations.
It opposed a creamy layer within SC/ST reservations.
31.x: In August 2026, the Centre was noted as opposing the introduction of a creamy layer for SCs and STs.
31.tq: Test the policy position rather than the general concept of reservation.
xs: In **Aug 2026** the Centre **opposed creamy layer for SC/ST** — option **(4)** is correct.
It neither supported a creamy layer nor proposed abolition of SC/ST quotas.
xa: **Bihar's 85%** proposal (2025) revived the **50% ceiling** debate.
The **Punjab & Haryana HC** struck down **Haryana's 75%** local quota.

31.s: Article 371-K was proposed for:
31.x: Article 371-K was proposed for Ladakh in September 2026.
31.tq: Discriminate between the State associated with a bill and the Union Territory associated with a constitutional proposal.
xs: **Art. 371-K** was proposed for **Ladakh** (**Sep 2026**) — option **(3)** is correct.
**Assam** is in news for the **UCC Bill, 2026**; **Bihar** for the **85%** quota proposal.
xa: The Assam UCC Bill is the **first in the North-East**, third State overall.
AP's renaming item: **Jonnagiri** → **Swarnagiri Gold Mine** (CDCA Jul 2026).

31.s: In August 2026, Andhra Pradesh fixed what share of reservation for Backward Classes in urban local body polls?
31.x: G.O. Rt. No. 1065 of 19 Aug 2026 provides a 33.33% BC quota in ULB polls. 27% and 34% are not the share fixed by the G.O., and 50% is the reservation ceiling under debate, not the ULB quota.
31.tq: AP ULB BC quota = 33.33% (G.O. 1065, Aug 2026).
xs: AP fixed a **33.33% BC quota in ULB polls** — option **(1)** is correct.
It was ordered by **G.O. Rt. No. 1065** dated **19 Aug 2026**.
**50%** is the reservation **ceiling** under debate, not the ULB quota.
xa: Other AP items: **Amaravati** made sole capital by Parliament (**2026**).
The AP Assembly passed a **Jan Vishwas Bill** and a **Fire Service (Amendment) Bill** (**Mar 2026**).

31.s:
With reference to the Presidential Reference on the Governor's assent, consider the following statements:
1. It was considered by a five-judge Constitution Bench.
2. The Reference concerned Articles 200 and 201.
3. The Court approved the concept of deemed assent when the Governor fails to act within a fixed period.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
31.x: The Presidential Reference was heard by a five-judge Constitution Bench and concerned the Governor's and President's powers under Articles 200 and 201. The Court rejected deemed assent and fixed judicial timelines.
31.tq: Find the statement that reverses the Court's express rejection of deemed assent.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: a **5-judge** Constitution Bench (Nov 2025) heard the Reference (**Art. 143**).
Statement 2 is correct: it concerned **Art. 200** (Governor) and **Art. 201** (President).
Statement 3 is wrong: **"deemed assent" was rejected** — so option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
xa: The Governor has **three options** under Art. 200; **no indefinite inaction**.
**Art. 142** cannot replace the Governor's role.
⚠ **5-judge** = assent reference; **9-judge** = "industry"; **7-judge** = legislative privileges.

31.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the ruling on the Governor's assent to Bills?
o: The Governor is required to decide every Bill within 30 days.
Article 142 authorises the Court to substitute its decision for that of the Governor.
The Court may grant deemed assent if the Governor does not act within a fixed period.
There are no court-imposed fixed timelines, but limited mandamus may issue for prolonged and unexplained inaction.
31.x: The Court held that the expression 'as soon as possible' does not create fixed judicial timelines. However, limited mandamus may be issued against prolonged and unexplained inaction; deemed assent and substitution under Article 142 were rejected.
31.tq: Separate the Court's limited supervisory power from an impermissible substitution of constitutional authorities.
xs: There are **no court-imposed fixed timelines**, but courts may issue **limited mandamus** against **prolonged, unexplained inaction** — option **(4)** is correct.
The text says **"as soon as possible"**, so no fixed period (like 30 days) can be imposed.
**Deemed assent** was **rejected**, and **Art. 142** cannot replace the Governor's role.
xa: The ruling came from a **5-judge** Bench (Nov 2025) on a Presidential Reference under **Art. 143**.
The Governor has **three options** under **Art. 200**.

31.s: In ADR v. ECI, the Supreme Court upheld the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls primarily as a power flowing from:
o: Article 143 and the Citizenship Act, 1955 only
Article 324 and the Representation of the People Act, 1950
Article 356 and the Representation of the People Act, 1951
31.x: The Court held that the Election Commission's power to conduct Special Intensive Revision flows from Article 324 of the Constitution and the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
31.tq: Identify the correct constitutional provision and statutory source instead of a neighbouring provision.
xs: In **ADR v. ECI** (Jun 2026), the SC upheld **SIR** as flowing from **Article 324** and the **Representation of the People Act, 1950** (**RP Act, 1950**) — option **(3)** is correct.
**Art. 200** concerns Governor's assent; **Art. 143** the Presidential Reference.
xa: The ECI may examine citizenship (**s.16 RPA 1950**).
SIR rules: max **1,200 voters per booth**; SC let **Aadhaar** be an identity document (**Sep 2025**).
AP draft rolls flagged **44,89,512** absent/shifted/dead/duplicate entries.

31.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Special Intensive Revision upheld in ADR v. ECI is correct?
o: The Election Commission cannot examine citizenship in the course of revision.
Exclusion from the electoral roll conclusively declares a person to be a non-citizen.
The Election Commission may examine citizenship, but exclusion from the roll is not a declaration of non-citizenship.
Only the Supreme Court may refer doubtful cases to the Central Government.
31.x: The Court recognised the Election Commission's power to examine citizenship during revision, while clarifying that exclusion from electoral rolls does not amount to a declaration of non-citizenship.
31.tq: Distinguish an electoral-roll consequence from the separate legal determination of citizenship.
xs: The **ECI may examine citizenship**, but **exclusion from rolls is not a declaration of non-citizenship** — option **(3)** is correct.
Doubtful cases go to the **Centre** under the **Citizenship Act 1955** — not referred by the SC, so option (4) is wrong.
xa: The ECI's power flows from **Art. 324** and the **RP Act, 1950**.
**SIR** exclusions are among the year's criticised issues.

31.s: Doubtful citizenship cases arising during the Special Intensive Revision are to be referred to the Central Government under the:
31.x: Doubtful cases may be referred to the Central Government under the Citizenship Act, 1955. The electoral revision power itself is linked to Article 324 and the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
31.tq: Use the statute-specific trap by separating the revision law from the citizenship law.
xs: Doubtful cases are referred to the Centre under the **Citizenship Act 1955** — option **(4)** is correct.
The revision power itself flows from **Art. 324** and the **RP Act, 1950**; citizenship is examined under **s.16 RPA 1950**.
xa: Exclusion from the rolls is **not** a declaration of non-citizenship.
The **SIR** verdict (**Jun 2026**) is among the year's biggest polity events.

31.s: Talaq-e-Hasan was challenged before the Supreme Court under which combination of Articles?
31.x: The challenge to Talaq-e-Hasan invoked Articles 14, 15 and 21. Instant triple talaq, or talaq-e-biddat, had already been struck down in Shayara Bano in 2017.
31.tq: Match the challenged practice with the exact constitutional provisions cited.
xs: **Talaq-e-Hasan** (**Benazeer Heena v. UoI**, 2025) was challenged under **Articles 14, 15 and 21** — option **(3)** is correct.
The case is still **pending**.
xa: Instant triple talaq (**talaq-e-biddat**) was struck down in **Shayara Bano (2017)**.
PYQ: after triple talaq (**2017**), **Talaq-e-Hasan** was the form challenged in the SC.

31.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Talaq-e-Hasan — form unrelated to the challenge under Articles 14, 15 and 21
Talaq-e-biddat — challenged form in Benazeer Heena v. Union of India
Talaq-e-Hasan — form struck down in Shayara Bano, 2017
Talaq-e-biddat — form struck down in Shayara Bano, 2017
31.x: Shayara Bano (2017) struck down instant triple talaq, known as talaq-e-biddat. Talaq-e-Hasan was subsequently challenged in Benazeer Heena v. Union of India.
31.tq: Discriminate between the two similarly named forms of talaq and their case history.
xs: **Talaq-e-biddat** (instant triple talaq) was struck down in **Shayara Bano, 2017** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Talaq-e-Hasan** is the form challenged in **Benazeer Heena v. UoI** under **Arts. 14, 15, 21** — so options (1), (2) and (3) are wrong.
xa: The Talaq-e-Hasan case is **pending**.
The **Sabarimala** reference judgment was **reserved** after **16** days of hearing (May 2026).

31.s: The Supreme Court's September 2025 direction relating to firecrackers called for:
o: A prohibition applicable only during religious festivals
A nationwide firecracker policy extending beyond Delhi-NCR
A policy limited exclusively to Delhi-NCR
A complete nationwide ban on all firecrackers
31.x: In September 2025, the Supreme Court called for a nationwide firecracker policy and indicated that restrictions should go beyond Delhi-NCR. The direction was not an absolute nationwide ban on all firecrackers.
31.tq: Avoid the extreme-word trap by distinguishing a nationwide policy from a total ban.
xs: In **Sep 2025** the SC called for a **nationwide firecracker policy**, with bans going **beyond Delhi-NCR** — option **(2)** is correct.
It was a call for a policy, not a **complete ban** on all firecrackers, and not limited to **Delhi-NCR** or festivals.
xa: Asked before: the SC **banned barium** in firecrackers across India (**Nov 2023**).
**S. Rajaseekaran v. UoI** (7 Oct 2025) gave pedestrian-safety directions.

31.s: S. Rajaseekaran v. Union of India, decided on 7 October 2025, is associated with directions concerning:
31.x: S. Rajaseekaran v. Union of India concerned pedestrian-safety directions. The Andhra Pradesh policy of 2026 was stated to build on this decision.
31.tq: Link the case name and date to the subject of its directions.
xs: **S. Rajaseekaran v. UoI** (**7 Oct 2025**) gave **pedestrian-safety** directions — option **(3)** is correct.
AP's pedestrian policy of **2026** builds on it.
Electoral-roll revision is **ADR v. ECI**; waqf is the **Waqf (Amendment) Act** order; tribunals is **Madras Bar Association**.
xa: The SC stayed the **UGC equity regulations, 2026** (**Apr 2026**).
The **Sabarimala** reference judgment was **reserved** after **16** days of hearing (May 2026).

31.s: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the definition of 'industry'?
o: The issue was decided by the Election Commission under Article 324.
The 1978 Bangalore Water Supply definition automatically applies to the Industrial Relations Code, 2020.
A nine-judge Bench headed by CJI Surya Kant held in August 2026 that the 1978 definition does not apply to the Industrial Relations Code, 2020.
A five-judge Bench held in November 2025 that the Industrial Relations Code is unconstitutional.
31.x: In August 2026, a nine-judge Bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant held that the 1978 Bangalore Water Supply definition does not apply to the Industrial Relations Code, 2020.
31.tq: Use the bench, date and holding together to reject swapped-case alternatives.
xs: A **9-judge** Bench headed by **CJI Surya Kant** (Aug 2026) held the **1978 Bangalore Water Supply** definition does **not** apply to the **Industrial Relations Code, 2020** — option **(3)** is correct.
The **5-judge** Bench of Nov 2025 dealt with the **Governor's assent** reference; **Art. 324** concerns the ECI.
xa: ⚠ **5-judge** = assent reference; **9-judge** = "industry"; **7-judge** = legislative privileges (**Art. 194(3)**).
The IRC absorbed the **ID Act 1947** and the **Trade Unions Act 1926**.

31.s:
Consider the following statements about the Supreme Court's May 2026 ruling on the appointment of the CEC and ECs:
1. The CJI's place on the selection panel under Anoop Baranwal (2023) was only an interim arrangement.
2. Under the 2023 Act, the selection panel consists of the PM, the Leader of the Opposition and the CJI.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
31.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Court held that the CJI's inclusion in Anoop Baranwal (2023) was only an interim arrangement. Statement 2 is wrong: the 2023 Act panel is the PM, the LoP and a Union Minister, not the CJI. So A; B and C wrongly accept statement 2, and D wrongly rejects statement 1.
31.tq: 2023 Act panel = PM + LoP + a Union Minister; the CJI's seat was only interim.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the **CJI's** place on the panel under **Anoop Baranwal (2023)** was only an **interim arrangement** (SC, May 2026).
Statement 2 is wrong: the **2023 Act** panel is the **PM, LoP and a Union Minister**, not the CJI — so option **(1) 1 only** is correct.
xa: CEC **Gyanesh Kumar** led the **IIC-DEM 2026** conference.
In **ADR v. ECI**, the ECI's SIR power was traced to **Art. 324**.

31.s: Which of the following cases was associated with striking down parts of the Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021?
o: Madras Bar Association v. Union of India
Benazeer Heena v. Union of India
S. Rajaseekaran v. Union of India
ADR v. Election Commission of India
31.x: Madras Bar Association v. Union of India was associated with the striking down of parts of the Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021.
31.tq: Match the case name with the legislation directly affected by the judgment.
xs: **Madras Bar Association v. UoI** (2025) struck down parts of the **Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Benazeer Heena** is the **Talaq-e-Hasan** case; **S. Rajaseekaran** concerns **pedestrian safety**; **ADR v. ECI** upheld **SIR**.
xa: The **Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026** replaces the 2021 Act and sets up a **National Tribunals Commission** (HQ New Delhi, **5** members).
Commission tenure: **5 years or age 70**.

31.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Legislative privileges — Seven-judge Bench under Article 194(3)
NALSAR row — Bar Council's power to punish law students upheld
UGC equity regulations, 2026 — stayed by the Supreme Court in April 2026
EVM totalisers — Supreme Court sought the Centre's view in September 2026
31.x: The NALSAR row concerned the proposition that the Bar Council has no power to punish law students, not that such power was upheld. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
31.tq: Find the single reversed holding in a group of closely related current judicial matters.
xs: In the **NALSAR** row (**Sep 2026**), the position is that the **Bar Council has no power to punish law students** — so pair **(2)** is NOT correctly matched.

The other pairs are correct: **7-judge** Bench on legislative privileges (**Art. 194(3)**); **UGC equity regulations, 2026** stayed (**Apr 2026**); Centre's view sought on **EVM totalisers** (**Sep 2026**).
xa: The SC also stayed parts of the **Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025** (Sep 2025).
The **Sabarimala** reference is reserved before a larger Bench.

31.s: Which of the following correctly states the Supreme Court’s interim directions of September 2025 concerning waqf provisions?
o: The five-year-practice rule and the Collector’s power were stayed; non-Muslim members were capped at three in State Boards and four in the Central Council.
Only the UMEED portal was stayed, while the five-year-practice rule was upheld without limitation.
All provisions of the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025 were permanently struck down.
The Collector’s power was transferred to State Boards and non-Muslim membership was capped at four in State Boards and three in the Council.
31.x: The interim order stayed the five-year-practice rule and the Collector’s power, and capped non-Muslim members at three in State Boards and four in the Council.
31.tq: Separate an interim stay and membership cap from permanent invalidation or transfer of powers.
xs: The **Sep 2025** interim order **stayed the 5-year-practice rule** and the **Collector's power** to decide waqf land, and capped non-Muslims at **3** on State boards and **4** on the **Central Waqf Council** — option **(1)** is correct.
Option (4) reverses the caps; option (3) is wrong as it was an **interim** order, not a permanent strike-down.
xa: ⚠ Remember **3** = State boards, **4** = Central Waqf Council.
The SC stayed the **UGC equity regulations, 2026** in **Apr 2026**.

31.s: In November 2023, the Supreme Court issued which order relating to firecrackers?
o: It banned the use of barium in firecrackers across India.
It banned all firecrackers across India.
It confined firecracker restrictions to Delhi-NCR only.
It permitted barium-based firecrackers across India.
31.x: The SC banned barium in firecrackers across India in Nov 2023 (asked before). It did not ban all firecrackers; in Sep 2025 it went further and called for a nationwide policy beyond Delhi-NCR, so 'Delhi-NCR only' is wrong; option D reverses the ban.
31.tq: Nov 2023: barium banned in crackers nationwide.
xs: In **Nov 2023** the SC **banned barium in firecrackers across India** (asked before) — option **(1)** is correct.
It did not ban all firecrackers; option (4) reverses the order.
xa: In **Sep 2025** the SC called for a **nationwide firecracker policy**, with bans beyond **Delhi-NCR**.

31.s:

31.x: Statement 1 is correct: SC e-Committee + NIC. Statement 2 is correct: 30 virtual courts for petty offences. Statement 3 is wrong: the SC is fully virtual on Mondays and Fridays. So A; B, C and D include the false statement 3.

xs: Statement 1 is correct: the **e-Courts Mission Mode Project** is run by the **SC e-Committee + NIC**.
Statement 2 is correct: it has **30 virtual courts** for petty offences.
Statement 3 is wrong: the SC is fully virtual on **Mondays and Fridays** — so option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
xa: SC initiatives: **"One Case One Data"** + **"Su Sahayak"** (**May 2026**); draft AI rules (**Jun 2026**).
**Four** new Division Benches came in **Jul 2026**.

31.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. One Case One Data — Supreme Court initiative
2. Su Sahayak — launched by the Supreme Court
3. Draft rules on AI in judiciary — June 2026
4. Four new Division Benches — July 2026
31.x: All four statements are correct. The Supreme Court launched One Case One Data and Su Sahayak in May 2026, issued draft AI rules in June 2026 and added four Division Benches in July 2026.
31.tq: Confirm each date-and-initiative pair before choosing the complete combination.
xs: All four pairs are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
The SC launched **"One Case One Data"** and **"Su Sahayak"** (**May 2026**).
It issued **draft rules on AI in judiciary** (**Jun 2026**) and set up **four new Division Benches** (**Jul 2026**).

31.s: According to the India Justice Report 2025, which one of the following correctly represents the judicial infrastructure indicators?
o: About 15 judges per million people, fewer than 2,600 vacancies and over 5.5 crore pending cases
About 25 judges per million people, more than 5,600 vacancies and over 3.5 crore pending cases
About 15 judges per million people, more than 5,600 vacancies and over 5.5 crore pending cases
About 10 judges per million people, more than 7,600 vacancies and over 4.5 crore pending cases
31.x: The India Justice Report 2025 records approximately 15 judges per million people, more than 5,600 vacancies and over 5.5 crore pending cases.
31.tq: Compare all three numerical indicators as a single data set.
xs: The **India Justice Report 2025** shows ~**15 judges per million**, **5,600+** vacancies and **5.5 crore+** pending cases — option **(3)** is correct.
Option (1) gets the vacancies wrong; options (2) and (4) change the judge ratio.
xa: **Fast-track courts**: **884** in **21** States/UTs with **17.54 lakh** pending cases.

31.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Collegium system is correct?
o: It is expressly provided in the Constitution and was established in 1950.
It was created by the 99th Constitutional Amendment and replaced by the NJAC in 2015.
It was established through an Act of Parliament in 1998.
It is not expressly mentioned in the Constitution and emerged through the Three Judges Cases, including the 1998 judgment.
31.x: The Collegium system is not expressly provided in the Constitution; it evolved through the Three Judges Cases, including the 1998 decision. The NJAC created by the 99th Amendment was struck down in 2015.
31.tq: Separate constitutional text from judicially evolved practice.
xs: The **Collegium** is **not in the Constitution**; it emerged from the **Three Judges Cases** (**1998**) — option **(4)** is correct.
So it was neither expressly provided in **1950** nor created by an Act of Parliament.
xa: CJI: **Surya Kant**.
The **India Justice Report 2025** counts ~**15** judges per million and **5,600+** vacancies.

31.s: According to the Union Law Minister (August 2026), how many fast-track courts were functioning in India?
31.x: There were 884 fast-track courts in 21 States/UTs, with 17.54 lakh cases pending (Aug 2026). The other options change either the number of courts or the number of States/UTs.
31.tq: FTCs: 884 courts, 21 States/UTs, 17.54 lakh pending.
xs: There are **884** fast-track courts in **21** States/UTs (Law Minister, **Aug 2026**) — option **(1)** is correct.
They have **17.54 lakh** pending cases.
xa: **India Justice Report 2025**: ~**15** judges per million; **5.5 crore+** pending cases.
AP: **137** of **875** judicial posts vacant.

31.s:
Consider the following statements about judicial infrastructure in Andhra Pradesh:

2. 10 court complexes are complete and 24 are under way, tracked on the Nyaya Vikas portal.

31.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: ₹104.29 crore in 5 years; 10 complexes done and 24 under way on Nyaya Vikas. Statement 3 is wrong: 137 of 875 posts are vacant, far less than half. So B; A misses statement 2, C and D include the false statement 3.
31.tq: AP courts: ₹104.29 cr; 10 + 24 complexes; 137/875 vacant.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: AP got **₹104.29 crore** central aid in **5** years.
Statement 2 is correct: **10** court complexes done, **24** under way, tracked on the **Nyaya Vikas** portal.
Statement 3 is wrong: only **137** of **875** posts are vacant — far less than half; option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.

**Fast-track courts** nationally: **884** in **21** States/UTs.

31.s: Bihar became the first State to adopt mobile e-voting for which elections?

31.s: Under the nationwide Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls beginning in 2025, the maximum number of voters per polling booth was specified as:
31.x: The nationwide Special Intensive Revision specified a maximum of 1,200 voters per booth.
31.tq: Recall the exact administrative ceiling and reject nearby rounded figures.
xs: The nationwide **SIR** set a maximum of **1,200 voters per booth** — option **(3)** is correct.

AP's draft rolls flagged **44,89,512** absent/shifted/dead/duplicate entries.

31.s:
With reference to the nationwide Special Intensive Revision, consider the following statements:
1. The Supreme Court permitted Aadhaar to be used as an identity document.
2. Electronic Voting Machines were to display colour photographs of candidates.
3. Aadhaar was declared conclusive proof of citizenship for electoral purposes.

31.x: The Supreme Court permitted Aadhaar to be used as an identity document, and EVMs were to display colour photographs of candidates. Aadhaar was not declared conclusive proof of citizenship.

xs: Statement 1 is correct: the SC let **Aadhaar** be used as an **identity document** (**Sep 2025**).
Statement 2 is correct: EVMs are to show **colour photos** of candidates.
Statement 3 is wrong: Aadhaar is an identity document, not proof of citizenship — so option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.

Max **1,200** voters per booth under the SIR.

31.s: A citizen wishes to report a suspected violation of the election code, a candidate seeks permission for an election-related activity, and a voter with disability seeks accessible voter services. Which sequence of applications is appropriate?

**QR-code ID cards** for counting centres from **4 May 2026**.

31.s: Registered Unrecognised Political Parties (RUPPs) are associated with which combination?

31.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the result of the Bihar Assembly election held in November 2025?

xs: Statement 1 is correct: **nominated** members of Parliament vote for the VP.

The **Assam UCC Bill, 2026** is the first UCC Bill in the **North-East**.

The resignation of the Education Minister

The formation of IIIDEM and the 2025 Labour Codes
