**UCC** is an **Assam** Bill; **SHANTI** and **Public Examinations** are Union laws.
xa: **Amaravati** was made sole capital by Parliament (**2026**).
AP State-level ordinances (**Art. 213**): **Human Organ Transplantation** (Jun 2026) and a **Sri City University** ordinance.

38.s:
Consider the following statements about the Urban Infrastructure Development Fund (UIDF):
1. It was announced in Budget 2023-24.
2. It is funded from the priority-sector-lending shortfall and run by NABARD.
3. It is meant for Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
38.x: Statement 1 is correct: UIDF was announced in Budget 2023-24. Statement 2 is wrong: it is funded from the PSL shortfall but run by the National Housing Bank, not NABARD. Statement 3 is correct: it is for Tier-2/3 cities. So B; A, C and D include the false statement 2.
38.tq: UIDF = Budget 2023-24, PSL shortfall, NHB, Tier-2/3 cities.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **UIDF** was announced in **Budget 2023-24**.
Statement 2 is wrong: it is funded from the **PSL shortfall** but run by the **National Housing Bank**, not NABARD.
Statement 3 is correct: it is for **Tier-2/3 cities** — so option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
xa: It carries **₹10,000 crore** a year; **₹30,000 crore** in total for **FY24-FY26**.
**AP** has taken about **₹4,000 crore** (**18 Aug 2026**); UIDF was asked in **2024**.

38.s:
Consider the following statements about the CBDC-based DBT pilot (August 2026):
1. Food subsidy under PM-GKAY was paid as purpose-bound e-rupee tokens.
2. The pilots were run in Delhi and Puducherry.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
38.x: Statement 1 is correct: PM-GKAY subsidy was paid as purpose-bound e-rupee tokens. Statement 2 is wrong: the pilots were in Chandigarh and Dadra & Nagar Haveli. So A; B and C wrongly accept statement 2, and D wrongly rejects statement 1.
38.tq: CBDC DBT pilot = PM-GKAY, Chandigarh + Dadra & Nagar Haveli.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **PM-GKAY** food subsidy was paid as purpose-bound **e₹** tokens (**CBDC-based DBT**).
Statement 2 is wrong: the pilots were in **Chandigarh** and **Dadra & Nagar Haveli** — so option **(1) 1 only**.
xa: The RBI is exploring a **"Kill Switch"** for digital payments (**2 Jun 2026**).
RBI tools: **MuleHunter.ai**, **ULI**, **DPIP**.

38.s: Under the Draft RBI (Interest Rates on Loans and Advances) Directions, 2026, floating-rate personal and MSME loans must use:
o: The marginal cost of funds only
The bank’s fixed prime lending rate
38.x: Floating-rate personal and MSME loans must use an external benchmark from 1 April 2027.
38.tq: Identify the prescribed benchmark and avoid substituting older internal benchmark terminology.
xs: Floating-rate personal + MSME loans must use an **external benchmark** — option **(2)** is correct.
This applies from **1 Apr 2027** under the **Draft RBI (Interest Rates on Loans and Advances) Directions, 2026** (**14 Aug 2026**).
xa: **Gross NPAs** hit a **decade-low 2.3%** (**Mar 2025**).

38.s: The four RRBs merged into one Andhra Pradesh bank have their headquarters at:
38.x: The merged Andhra Pradesh RRB has its headquarters at Guntur.
38.tq: Apply the location filter to distinguish the headquarters from other major cities in the State.
xs: The merged AP **RRB** (four RRBs into one) has its HQ at **Guntur** — option **(1)** is correct.
Its **first anniversary** was in **May 2026**.
xa: AP's retail inflation (**4.9%**) is above the national rate.
AP has taken about **₹4,000 crore** from the **UIDF**.

38.s: India’s gross non-performing assets reached a decade-low level of 2.3 per cent in:
38.x: Gross NPAs stood at a decade-low 2.3% in March 2025.
38.tq: Link the percentage to the specific reference month and year.
xs: **Gross NPAs** fell to a **decade-low 2.3%** in **Mar 2025** (**March 2025**) — option **(4)** is correct.
It is listed under **asset quality** among RBI banking developments; the notes give no such figure for **2023**, **2024** or **2026**.
xa: RBI tools: **MuleHunter.ai**, **ULI**, **DPIP**.
Four RRBs were merged into one **AP** bank (HQ **Guntur**).

38.s: Which one of the following is NOT listed as an asset-quality or financial-sector technology tool?
38.x: MuleHunter.ai, ULI and DPIP are listed as tools related to asset quality or financial-sector development. PaSS is a Payments Vision 2028 initiative.
38.tq: Separate banking and asset-quality tools from payment-system initiatives.
xs: **PaSS** (**Payments Switching Service**) is a **Payments Vision 2028** initiative, not one of the listed tools — option **(3)** is correct.
**MuleHunter.ai**, **ULI** and **DPIP** are listed as RBI tools.
xa: **Payments Vision 2028** (Apr 2026) has **15 initiatives**, including white-label **AePS**.
It provides **shared liability** of sender and receiver banks for fraud.

38.s:
Consider the following statements about the RBI's Payments Vision 2028 (April 2026):
1. It has 15 initiatives.
2. It provides for shared liability of sender and receiver banks for fraud.
3. It removes RBI oversight of e-commerce marketplaces.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
38.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Vision has 15 initiatives. Statement 2 is correct: sender and receiver banks share fraud liability. Statement 3 is wrong: it brings in RBI oversight of e-commerce marketplaces. So A; B, C and D include the false statement 3.
38.tq: Payments Vision 2028 = 15 initiatives, shared fraud liability, PaSS, white-label AePS.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Payments Vision 2028** has **15 initiatives**.
Statement 2 is correct: **sender and receiver banks share fraud liability**.
Statement 3 is wrong: it brings in **RBI oversight of e-commerce marketplaces** — so option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
xa: It also includes **PaSS** and **white-label AePS**.
The RBI is exploring a **"Kill Switch"** for digital payments.

38.s: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the issue of currency in India?
o: The Government of India issues banknotes and the RBI issues coins.
The RBI issues banknotes under Section 22 of the RBI Act, while coins are issued by the Government of India under the Coinage Act, 2011.
Both banknotes and coins are issued exclusively by the RBI.
Both banknotes and coins are issued exclusively by the Ministry of Finance under the RBI Act.
38.x: Banknotes are issued by the RBI under Section 22 of the RBI Act, whereas coins are issued by the Government of India under the Coinage Act, 2011.
38.tq: Apply the 'who would do this job?' method to distinguish note and coin authorities.
xs: **Banknotes** are issued by the **RBI** under **Section 22** of the RBI Act; **coins** by the **Government of India** under the **Coinage Act, 2011** — option **(2)** is correct.
Options (1), (3) and (4) mix up the two issuers.
xa: ⚠ Banknotes = **RBI**; coins = **Government of India**.
**Sec. 45ZB**, RBI Act creates the **MPC**; **Sec. 45ZA** sets the inflation target (**4% ± 2%**).
**Demonetisation** (**8 Nov 2016**) covered **₹500 and ₹1,000** notes.

38.s: Demonetisation of the ₹500 and ₹1,000 notes was announced by the Government of India on:
38.x: The Government announced demonetisation of the ₹500 and ₹1,000 notes on 8 November 2016.
38.tq: Distinguish the exact announcement date from nearby November dates.
xs: **Demonetisation** of the **₹500 and ₹1,000** notes was announced by the Government on **8 Nov 2016** (**8 November 2016**) — option **(2)** is correct.
The other dates are not in the notes for this event.
xa: ⚠ Banknotes are issued by the **RBI** (**Section 22**, RBI Act); coins by the **Government of India** (**Coinage Act, 2011**).
**UPI** was launched earlier that year, on **11 April 2016**.
**BHIM** also dates from **2016**.

38.s: The interest rate on EPF deposits for 2025-26 was fixed at:
38.x: The EPF interest rate for 2025-26 was 8.25 per cent and remained unchanged.
38.tq: Distinguish the EPF rate from the nearby small-savings rates.
xs: The **EPF rate for 2025-26** is **8.25%** (unchanged) — option **(2)**, **8.25 per cent**, is correct.
**7.1%** is the **PPF** rate.
xa: Recommended by the EPFO **Central Board of Trustees** on **2 Mar 2026**; approved by the **Finance Ministry**.
**₹1.44 lakh crore** credited to **34 crore** accounts on **15 Jul 2026**.
⚠ **EPF 8.25%** vs **SSY 8.2%** (highest small-savings rate).

38.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the EPF contribution structure?
o: 10 per cent by the employee and 12 per cent by the employer
12 per cent by the employee and 12 per cent by the employer
8.25 per cent by the employee and 8.25 per cent by the employer
12 per cent by the employee and 8.25 per cent by the employer
38.x: The EPF contribution remains 12 per cent from the employee and 12 per cent from the employer.
38.tq: Separate the contribution percentages from the interest rate.
xs: The EPF contribution stays **12% + 12%** — employee and employer — option **(2)** is correct.
**8.25%** is the EPF **interest rate**, not a contribution share.
xa: EPF interest for **2025-26**: **8.25%** (unchanged).
Recommended by the **Central Board of Trustees** on **2 Mar 2026**.
**34 crore** accounts credited on **15 Jul 2026**.

38.s:
Consider the following statements about small-savings schemes:
1. Their rates remained unchanged for the eighth consecutive quarter from 1 April 2026.
2. The rates are set quarterly by the Finance Ministry.
3. The rates are linked to Government securities yields.
4. The funds are credited to the National Small Savings Fund in the Public Account.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
38.x: All four statements are correct. Small-savings rates were unchanged for the eighth straight quarter, are set quarterly by the Finance Ministry, linked to G-Sec yields and credited to the National Small Savings Fund in the Public Account.
38.tq: Test the full institutional chain rather than only the interest figures.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: rates **unchanged** for the **8th straight quarter** from **1 Apr 2026**.
Statements 2 and 3 are correct: set **quarterly** by the **Finance Ministry**, linked to **G-Sec** yields.
Statement 4 is correct: money goes to the **National Small Savings Fund** (**Public Account**) — so **1, 2, 3 and 4**, option **(4)**.

38.s: The 'Micro Bachat' micro-insurance plan was launched by:
38.x: LIC launched the 'Micro Bachat' micro-insurance plan.
38.tq: Use the organisation-product association directly.
xs: **LIC** launched the **'Micro Bachat'** micro-insurance plan (**2019**) — option **(1)** is correct.
The **National Small Savings Fund** is a Public Account fund, and **EPFO** runs EPF — neither launched an insurance plan.
xa: Insurance penetration: **3.7%** (**ES 2025-26**).
**Sabka Bima Sabki Raksha Act, 2025**: **100% FDI in insurance**.
**Bharat Maritime Insurance Pool** launched **12 May 2026**.

38.s: Which pair of small-savings interest rates (Q1 FY27, unchanged from 1 April 2026) is correct?
38.x: SSY earns 8.2% and PPF 7.1%. Option B swaps them; 7.7% is the NSC rate, not PPF or SSY.
38.tq: SSY 8.2, PPF 7.1, NSC 7.7, PO savings 4.
xs: **Sukanya Samriddhi 8.2%; PPF 7.1%** (SSY is the highest small-savings rate) — option **(1)** is correct.
Option (2) swaps them; **7.7%** is the **NSC** rate.
xa: **3-year TD 7.1%**; **PO savings 4%**.
Rates **unchanged** for the **8th straight quarter** (from **1 Apr 2026**).

38.s:
Consider the following statements about India's external sector:
1. Russia supplied about 48% of India's crude imports in June 2026.
2. The US Senate was advancing a 50% tariff on buyers of Russian oil.
3. India's current account deficit in 2025-26 was 1.1% of GDP.
4. India's services exports fell by 15.3% in 2025-26.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
38.x: Statement 1 is correct: Russia was about 48% of crude imports in June 2026. Statement 2 is wrong: the US Senate was advancing a 100% tariff, not 50%. Statement 3 is correct: CAD was 1.1% of GDP in 2025-26. Statement 4 is wrong: services exports rose by 15.3%. So B; A and C include the false statement 2, and D includes the false statement 4.
38.tq: Russia 48% crude, 100% US tariff, CAD 1.1%, services exports UP 15.3%.

38.s: More than 75 per cent of India's FDI inflows in April 2026 came from which group of countries?
o: China, Russia and the United States
Japan, China and the United Kingdom
38.x: Japan, Singapore and Mauritius together accounted for over 75 per cent of India's FDI inflows in April 2026.
38.tq: Group the countries by their stated FDI relationship rather than by trade status.
xs: Over **75%** of **April 2026** FDI inflows came from **Japan, Singapore, Mauritius** — option **(2)** is correct.
**China** is India's biggest **trading partner**, not a top FDI source here.
xa: **Press Note 3** eased (**Mar 2026**): up to **10% Chinese** stake → automatic route.
**100% FDI in insurance** under the **Sabka Bima Sabki Raksha Act, 2025**.

38.s: Which factor was associated with the rise in CPI to 4.45% after the Q1 FY27 GDP rebasing?
o: Higher oil prices linked to the West Asia situation
A fall in domestic food production alone
The abolition of the repo rate
38.x: The rise in CPI to 4.45% was associated with West Asia-related oil-price pressures.
38.tq: Link the stated external shock with its inflationary effect.
xs: After rebasing, CPI rose to **4.45%** as **West Asia oil prices** bit (**Aug-Sep 2026**) — option **(1)** is correct.
GDP grew **7.8%** in Q1 FY27 at the same time; the notes link the CPI rise to oil, not to food alone, GST or the repo.
xa: Aug CPI of **4.8%** raised the odds of an **October 2026** rate hike.
**Russia** supplied **48%** of crude imports, rising since the West Asia war.

38.s: Which institutions were associated with loans relevant to Andhra Pradesh’s development initiatives?
o: World Bank through SALT and Asian Development Bank through VCIC
IMF through SALT and World Bank through VCIC
ADB through SALT and IMF through VCIC
UNDP through SALT and World Bank through GST 2.0
38.x: The World Bank was associated with SALT, while the Asian Development Bank was associated with VCIC loans.
38.tq: Match each acronym with the correct international financial institution.
xs: Loans for AP: the **World Bank's SALT** and **ADB's VCIC** — option **(1)** is correct.
The notes link neither SALT nor VCIC to the **IMF** or **UNDP**.
xa: AP's retail inflation (**4.9%**) is above the national rate.
AP net GST **2025-26** growth **6%** despite a **₹4,500 crore** GST 2.0 hit.
**UIDF**: AP has taken about **₹4,000 crore** (**18 Aug 2026**).

38.s: Which of the following statements reflects the current monetary and payments-related developments mentioned?
o: UPI MDR began in February 2025, and the August 2026 rate hike had already occurred.
UPI MDR was expected from 15 October 2026, and a rate hike was considered likely in October 2026.
UPI MDR was introduced with GST 2.0 in September 2025, and no policy change was expected.
UPI MDR was abolished from 15 October 2026, and a rate cut was certain in October 2026.
38.x: A change relating to UPI MDR was expected from 15 October 2026, while an October 2026 rate hike was considered likely after the inflation developments.
38.tq: Separate an expected future development from a completed policy action.
xs: **UPI MDR** starts from **15 Oct 2026**, and a **rate hike** was likely in **Oct 2026** — option **(2)** is correct.
The repo was **held at 5.25%** in **Aug 2026** (no hike yet); **Feb 2025** was a rate **cut**.
xa: Aug minutes hint at a hike; Aug CPI **4.8%**.
Stance **Neutral** since **Jun 2025**.

38.s:
Consider the following statements about Andhra Pradesh's economy:
1. AP's retail inflation (4.9%) was below the national rate.
2. AP's net GST collections grew 6% in 2025-26 despite a ₹4,500 crore hit from GST 2.0.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
38.x: Statement 1 is wrong: AP's retail inflation of 4.9% was above the national rate. Statement 2 is correct: net GST grew 6% in 2025-26 despite a ₹4,500 crore GST 2.0 hit. So B; A and C accept the false statement 1, and D rejects the true statement 2.
38.tq: AP: inflation 4.9% (above national); net GST +6% despite ₹4,500 cr hit.
xs: Statement 1 is wrong: AP's retail inflation (**4.9%**) was **above** the national rate.
Statement 2 is correct: AP net GST grew **6%** in **2025-26** despite a **₹4,500 crore** **GST 2.0** hit — so **2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: **World Bank's SALT** + **ADB's VCIC** loans for AP.
National CPI: **4.45%** in **Jul 2026**.

44.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes PMAY-G from PMAY-U?
o: PMAY-G is implemented by MoHUA, whereas PMAY-U is implemented by Rural Development.
PMAY-G concerns LPG and PMAY-U concerns electricity connections.
PMAY-G is implemented by Rural Development, whereas PMAY-U is implemented by MoHUA.
Both are implemented by the Ministry of Jal Shakti.
44.x: PMAY-G is associated with the Ministry of Rural Development, while PMAY-U is associated with the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs. Both concern pucca housing in rural and urban areas respectively.
44.tq: Compare the ministry and rural-urban scope instead of relying on similar abbreviations.
xs: **PMAY-G** (**2016**) is under **Rural Development**, whereas **PMAY-U** (**2015**) is under **MoHUA** — option **(3)** is correct.
Option (1) swaps the ministries; both give **pucca houses**, not LPG or electricity, and neither is under **Jal Shakti**.
xa: PMAY-G unit assistance: **₹1.20 lakh (plains) / ₹1.30 lakh (hilly)**.
More than **3 crore** rural houses done under PMAY-G.
**Saubhagya** (**2017**, Power) = electricity connection to every household.

44.s: PMKVY primarily provides:
o: Tap water connections to rural households
44.x: The Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana provides short-term skill training and certification and is associated with the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship.
44.tq: Match the scheme with its precise operational objective.
xs: **PMKVY** (**2015**, Skill Development & Entrepreneurship) provides **short-term skill training and certification** — option **(2)** is correct.
Electricity connections = **Saubhagya**; health cover = **PM-JAY**; tap water = **Jal Jeevan Mission**.
xa: **Skill India** certificates are mapped to **NSQF** and linked to **DigiLocker**.
**PM-SETU / ITI upgradation**: **₹60,000 crore** over **5** years, **1,000** ITIs.
**India-France** aeronautics skilling centre at **NSTI Kanpur** (**Jun 2026**).

44.s:
Consider the following statements about PM Ujjwala Yojana:
1. It is administered by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.
2. It was launched in May 2016.
3. Ujjwala 2.0 was introduced in 2019.
4. It gives deposit-free LPG connections to adult women of poor households.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
44.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct: PMUY is under Petroleum & Natural Gas, launched May 2016, and gives deposit-free LPG connections to adult women of poor households. Statement 3 is wrong: Ujjwala 2.0 came in 2021. So '1, 2 and 4 only'; '1 and 2 only' misses 4, and the options with 3 are wrong.
44.tq: Ujjwala: 2016 launch, 2.0 in 2021.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: **PMUY** is under **Petroleum & Natural Gas**, launched **May 2016**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Ujjwala 2.0** came in **2021**, not 2019.
Statement 4 is correct: **deposit-free LPG connection** to adult women of poor households — so **1, 2 and 4 only**, option **(4)**.
xa: **10.57 crore** connections; 2025-26 targeted subsidy **₹12,000 crore**.
⚠ **PMUY** = LPG **connection**; **PAHAL** = DBT of the LPG **subsidy**.
AP's **Deepam-2**: **3** free LPG cylinders a year alongside PMUY.

44.s: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY is associated with which ministry and implementing institution?
o: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and the National Health Authority
Ministry of Power and the National Skill Development Corporation
Ministry of Rural Development and SIDBI
Ministry of Jal Shakti and the Survey of India
44.x: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY is associated with the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and is implemented through the National Health Authority.
44.tq: Match the scheme with its parent ministry and implementing institution.
xs: **Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY** (**Sep 2018**) is under the **Ministry of Health and Family Welfare**, implemented by the **National Health Authority** — option **(1)** is correct.
**SIDBI** implements **PM SVANidhi**; the **Survey of India** does **SVAMITVA** drone surveys.
xa: Cover: **₹5 lakh** per family a year.
**Saubhagya** (**2017**) is under **Power**.

44.s: SVAMITVA uses drone surveys primarily to provide:
o: Property cards for rural abadi land
44.x: SVAMITVA uses drone surveys conducted by the Survey of India to provide property cards for rural abadi land.
44.tq: Identify the instrument, land category and resulting document in the scheme.
xs: **SVAMITVA** (**Apr 2020**, Panchayati Raj) uses drone surveys by the **Survey of India** to give **property cards for rural abadi land** — option **(2)** is correct.
LPG connections = **PMUY**; street-vendor loans = **PM SVANidhi**; health cover = **PM-JAY**.
xa: Target: **6.62 lakh villages**.
Launched **24 Apr 2020**, **National Panchayati Raj Day**.
**DILRMP 3.0** guidelines issued (**12 Sep 2026**).

44.s: Which scheme is correctly matched with its objective?
o: SVAMITVA — deposit-free LPG connection to adult women
PMKVY — ₹5 lakh health cover per poor family
PM-JAY — drone survey of rural abadi land
Saubhagya — electricity connection to every household
44.x: Saubhagya aims to provide electricity connections to every household. LPG connections, health cover and drone-based property cards are associated with PMUY, PM-JAY and SVAMITVA respectively.
44.tq: Find the correctly matched pair by separating the outputs of similar welfare schemes.
xs: **Saubhagya** (**2017**, Power) = **electricity connection to every household** — option **(4)** is correct.
Deposit-free LPG = **PMUY**; **₹5 lakh** cover = **PM-JAY**; drone survey of abadi land = **SVAMITVA**.
**PMKVY** is skill training, not health cover.
xa: PMUY: **10.57 crore** connections.
SVAMITVA target: **6.62 lakh villages**.
PM-JAY is implemented by the **National Health Authority**.

44.s: Under PMAY-G (Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Gramin), the unit assistance for building a pucca house is:
o: Rs 1.30 lakh in plains and Rs 1.20 lakh in hilly areas
Rs 1.20 lakh in plains and Rs 1.30 lakh in hilly areas
Rs 2.50 lakh uniformly in all areas
Rs 1.50 lakh in plains and Rs 2.00 lakh in hilly areas
44.x: PMAY-G gives Rs 1.20 lakh in plains and Rs 1.30 lakh in hilly areas (the higher amount for difficult terrain). Option A reverses the two; Rs 2.50 lakh uniform and Rs 1.50/2.00 lakh are not PMAY-G figures. PMAY-G (2016, Rural Development) has completed more than 3 crore rural houses.
44.tq: PMAY-G: 1.20 plains, 1.30 hills - hills get more.
xs: PMAY-G gives **₹1.20 lakh in plains and ₹1.30 lakh in hilly** areas (Rs 1.20 lakh in plains and Rs 1.30 lakh in hilly areas) — option **(2)** is correct.
Option (1) reverses the two amounts.
xa: PMAY-G (**2016**) is under **Rural Development**; PMAY-U (**2015**) under **MoHUA**.
More than **3 crore** rural houses completed.
Both give **pucca houses**.

44.s: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY provides health cover of:
o: Rs 1 lakh per family per year
Rs 5 lakh per individual per year
Rs 5 lakh per family per year
Rs 10 lakh per family over five years
44.x: PM-JAY (Sep 2018, Health & FW, implemented by the National Health Authority) gives Rs 5 lakh per family a year. The cover is per family (floater), not per individual; Rs 1 lakh and Rs 10 lakh over five years are wrong figures.
44.tq: PM-JAY = 5 lakh, per FAMILY, per YEAR.
xs: **PM-JAY** gives **₹5 lakh per family per year** (Rs 5 lakh per family per year) — option **(3)** is correct.
The cover is **per family**, not per individual.
xa: Launched **Sep 2018**; **Health & FW**, via the **National Health Authority**.
⚠ PMAY-G unit assistance (**₹1.20 / ₹1.30 lakh**) is a different figure.

44.s:
Consider the following statements about PM-KISAN:
1. It gives ₹6,000 a year in three instalments of ₹2,000.
2. Income-tax payers are eligible for its benefits.
3. It has been extended to 2030-31.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
44.x: Statement 1 is correct: ₹6,000/year in three ₹2,000 instalments. Statement 2 is wrong: income-tax payers and most government employees are excluded. Statement 3 is correct: PM-KISAN was extended to 2030-31. So '1 and 3 only'; '1 only' misses 3, and options with 2 are wrong.
44.tq: PM-KISAN exclusions: income-tax payers, most govt employees.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **₹6,000/yr** in **3 instalments of ₹2,000**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **income-tax payers** and most government employees are **excluded**.
Statement 3 is correct: extended to **2030-31** (**₹3.15 lakh crore**) — so **1 and 3 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: PM-KISAN (**2018**) covers all **landholding farmer families**.
It has paid **₹494.75 crore** in **NTR district**, AP (**26 Jun 2026**).
Extension announced **Aug 2026**.

44.s:
Consider the following statements about VB-G RAM G:
1. It provides 125 days of work to rural households.
2. Its interim base wage is ₹300 per day.
3. Wages are shared 50:50 between the Centre and States.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
44.x: Statement 1 is correct: 125 days of work. Statement 2 is correct: ₹300/day interim base wage. Statement 3 is wrong: wages are shared 60:40 Centre-State. So '1 and 2 only'; '1, 2 and 3' and '2 and 3 only' include the wrong statement, and '1 only' misses 2.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **125 days** of work for rural households.
Statement 2 is correct: interim base wage **₹300/day**.
Statement 3 is wrong: wages are shared **60:40** Centre-State — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(3)**.
xa: **VB-G RAM G** replaced **MGNREGA** on **1 Jul 2026**; the Act was passed in **Dec 2025**.
Wages indexed to **CPI-AL**.

44.s: The loan structure under PM SVANidhi is correctly represented by:
44.x: PM SVANidhi provides successive loans of ₹15,000, ₹25,000 and ₹50,000 to street vendors.
44.tq: Recall the ascending three-stage loan sequence exactly.
xs: **PM SVANidhi** loans: **₹15,000 → ₹25,000 → ₹50,000** — option **(1)** is correct.
It also gives a **7%** interest subsidy.
xa: For **street vendors**; started **2020**, extended to **Mar 2030**.
Implemented by **SIDBI**.

44.s:
Consider the following statements about PM SVANidhi:
1. It is meant for street vendors.
2. It provides a 7% interest subsidy.
3. The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs and the Department of Financial Services are associated with it.
4. SIDBI implements the scheme.

44.s:

44.s:

44.x: Statement 1 is correct: Khelo India began in 2018. Statement 2 is correct: Feeder Schools and Utkrishta Vidyalayas are new components of the Aug 2026 revamp. Statement 3 is wrong: the target is top-10 by 2036, not 2030. Hence '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses 2, and the options with 3 are wrong.

Statement 2 is correct: the **Aug 2026** revamp adds **Khelo India Feeder Schools** + **Utkrishta Vidyalayas**.

44.s:

xs: Statement 1 is correct: **MISHTI** = **Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats and Tangible Incomes**.
Statements 2 and 3 are correct: extended to **2029** with **₹500 crore** more, total **₹600 crore** (**17 Jul 2026**).

44.s: The revamped Khelo India scheme approved by the Cabinet in August 2026 has a total outlay, including the allocation for National Sports Federations, for 2026-27 to 2030-31 of:
44.x: The total is Rs 36,441 crore: Rs 29,054 crore for Khelo India plus Rs 7,387 crore for National Sports Federations. Rs 29,054 crore and Rs 7,387 crore are only the two parts; Rs 60,000 crore is the PM-SETU ITI outlay.

xs: The revamped **Khelo India** outlay is **₹36,441 crore** for **2026-27 to 2030-31** — so option **(4)** is correct.

44.s:

Statement 2: **Centre ₹30,000 crore + States ₹20,000 crore + industry ₹10,000 crore**.
Statements 3 and 4: the **World Bank and ADB** co-finance **50%** of the central share; **1,000** ITIs are grouped in **hub-and-spoke** clusters.

**NSQF** gives competency-based qualification levels; Skill India certificates are mapped to it and linked to **DigiLocker**.
India-France (**Jun 2026**): an **aeronautics skilling centre** at **NSTI Kanpur**.

44.s: Which of the following schemes is identified as World Bank-aided and intended for minority youth?
44.x: Nai Manzil is a World Bank-aided programme intended for minority youth. Atal Bhujal Yojana is also listed among World Bank-aided schemes, but has a different focus.

xs: **Nai Manzil** is the **World Bank-aided** scheme for **minority youth** — so option **(2)** is correct.

44.s: Under the Jal Jeevan Mission, a Centrally Sponsored Scheme, the Centre-State funding pattern is:
o: 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States, 50:50 for other States and 100% central for UTs without legislature
60:40 for all States and 100% central for all UTs
75:25 for North-Eastern States and 60:40 for other States
50:50 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States and 90:10 for other States
44.x: JJM funding: NE and Himalayan States 90:10, other States 50:50, UTs without legislature 100% central. 60:40 for all States is a common CSS pattern but not JJM's; 75:25 is not used; option D reverses the two ratios.
44.tq: Hills and NE get 90:10; others 50:50 (not 60:40).
xs: JJM funding is **90:10** for **NE and Himalayan** States, **50:50** for other States and **100%** central for **UTs without legislature** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**60:40** is the Centre-State wage share under **VB-G RAM G**, not JJM; option (4) reverses JJM's two ratios.
xa: ⚠ **VB-G RAM G** wages = **60:40**; **JJM** (others) = **50:50**; **VVP-II** = **100% central**.
**Jal Jeevan Mission** (**2019**, Jal Shakti) gives tap water (**FHTC**) to every rural household.

**Sujal Gaon ID / Sujalam Bharat** gives a digital ID to each rural water scheme under JJM 2.0.

44.s: CBDC-based DBT under PM-GKAY uses purpose-bound e₹ primarily for:

44.tq: Identify the purpose of the digital payment rather than the technology alone.
xs: **CBDC-based DBT** under **PM-GKAY** pays a **food subsidy** as purpose-bound digital rupee (**e₹**) — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **LPG subsidy** goes by **PAHAL** (DBT to an Aadhaar-seeded bank account), not by e₹.
It runs in **Chandigarh** and **Dadra & Nagar Haveli** (**2026**).
xa: The digital rupee here is **programmable** (purpose-bound), so it can be spent only on its purpose.
**JAM trinity** (Jan Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile) is the base of DBT; idea set out in **ES 2014-15**.
**PAHAL**: cylinder bought at market price, subsidy credited to the Aadhaar-seeded bank account.

44.s: Under PAHAL, the LPG subsidy is transferred when:
o: The subsidy is credited to the gas agency before delivery
The consumer pays a subsidised price and receives no subsequent transfer
The consumer receives the cylinder free of cost from the distributor
The consumer buys the cylinder at market price and the subsidy is credited to the Aadhaar-seeded bank account
44.x: Under PAHAL, the LPG cylinder is bought at market price and the subsidy is subsequently credited to the consumer’s Aadhaar-seeded bank account.
44.tq: Trace the sequence of purchase, subsidy credit and bank-account linkage.
xs: Under **PAHAL**, the consumer buys the LPG cylinder at **market price** and the subsidy is credited to the **Aadhaar-seeded bank account** — so option **(4)** is correct.
There is no subsidy paid to the gas agency, no subsidised counter price and no free cylinder: PAHAL is a **DBT** for LPG.
xa: ⚠ **PMUY** = deposit-free LPG **connection**; **PAHAL** = DBT of the LPG **subsidy**.
**PM Ujjwala Yojana** (**May 2016**): **10.57 crore** connections; **Ujjwala 2.0** in **2021**; 2025-26 targeted subsidy **₹12,000 crore**.
**JAM trinity** (Jan Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile) is the base of DBT.
AP's **Deepam-2** gives **3** free LPG cylinders a year alongside PMUY.

51.x: Statement 1 is correct: both indices are NITI Aayog's. Statement 2 is wrong: the Good Governance Index is published by DARPG. So '1 only'; '2 only', 'Both' and 'Neither' are wrong.
51.tq: Good Governance Index = DARPG, not NITI.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — so option **(1) 1 only** is the answer.
Statement 1 is correct: the **SDG India Index** and **Composite Water Management Index** are **NITI Aayog's**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the **Good Governance Index** is by **DARPG**.
xa: NITI Aayog also publishes **SEQI** and the **Health Index**.
Good Governance Index sectors include **grievance redressal** and **e-governance**.
NITI Aayog's **Fiscal Health Index 2026**: **Odisha** 1st, **Punjab** last.

51.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the criticism of the 16th Finance Commission award:
1. Revenue-deficit grants were dropped.
2. The weight assigned to income distance was reduced.
3. The changes were viewed as placing efficiency above equity.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
51.x: All three statements are correct: revenue-deficit grants were dropped, the income-distance weight was reduced, and the resulting approach was criticised for prioritising efficiency over equity.
51.tq: Check whether all linked features of a policy criticism are simultaneously present.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is the answer.
Statements 1 and 2: the **16th FC** dropped **revenue-deficit grants** and cut the **income-distance** weight.
Statement 3: critics say **efficiency** now counts over **equity** (**6 Aug 2026**).
xa: The 16th FC kept vertical devolution at **41%**.
New criterion: **contribution to GDP** (**10%**).
AP's devolution share rose **4.2%** under the 16th FC.

51.s: Which demand was pressed by Andhra Pradesh in relation to the criteria of the 16th Finance Commission?
51.x: Andhra Pradesh pressed for greater weight to capital needs in the Finance Commission criteria.
51.tq: Match the concerned State with its specific policy demand.
xs: AP pressed for **greater weight to capital needs** in the 16th FC criteria — so option **(4)** is correct (**Feb 2026**).
The notes record no AP demand to remove income distance, weight only population or abolish devolution.
xa: AP's devolution share rose **4.2%** under the 16th FC (**3 Feb 2026**).
The 16th FC award runs **1 Apr 2026 - 31 Mar 2031**.
It recommended **₹4.35 lakh crore** for gram panchayats.

51.s: Which State was reported to have secured a change in the VBSA framework relating to State consent?
51.x: Andhra Pradesh was reported to have secured the change relating to State consent in the VBSA framework.
51.tq: Match the State with the specific institutional change it secured.
xs: **Andhra Pradesh** won the **VBSA** change on **State consent** — so option **(3)** is correct (**18 Jul 2026**).
After AP objected, the Centre agreed that State consent is needed for decisions on colleges of State universities.
xa: In the JPC, **AP, Meghalaya and MP** objected to the centralising provisions.
The JPC (**31 members**) is chaired by **D. Purandeswari**.
The **VBSA Bill, 2025** would replace **UGC, AICTE, NCTE** with one regulator.

51.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The IMF gave India's national accounts a 'C' grade.
2. Delayed NCRB and AISHE data has been criticised.
3. Andhra Pradesh ranked 5th in the Fiscal Health Index.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
51.x: Statement 1 is correct: the IMF gave a 'C' grade. Statement 2 is correct: delayed NCRB/AISHE data is a listed criticism. Statement 3 is wrong: AP was 17th in the FHI; it was 5th in EPI 2024. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses 2, and options with 3 are wrong.
51.tq: AP: 5th in EPI, 17th in FHI.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — so option **(2) 1 and 2 only** is the answer.
Statement 1 is correct: the **IMF** gave India's national accounts a **"C"** grade.
Statement 2 is correct: delayed **NCRB**/**AISHE** data is a listed criticism.
Statement 3 is wrong: AP was **17th** in the **FHI**; it was **5th** in **EPI 2024**.
xa: **Odisha** was 1st among major states in the **FHI 2026**.
**AISHE** 2022-23 and 2023-24 showed **UG enrolment fell for the first time**.
AP's devolution share rose **4.2%** under the 16th FC.

51.s: Who was identified as the Chairman of the Andhra Pradesh State Scheduled Castes Commission in August 2026?
o: The Chairperson of the State Minorities Commission
51.x: K.S. Jawahar was identified as the Chairman of the Andhra Pradesh State Scheduled Castes Commission in August 2026.
51.tq: Match the person with the correct State commission rather than a similarly named national commission.
xs: **K.S. Jawahar** is the chair of the **AP SC Commission** (**Aug 2026**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Harjit Singh Grewal** chairs the national **NCM**; **Niranjan Jyoti** chairs the **NCBC**.
xa: National **NCSC** chair: **Kishor Makwana**.
The NCSC is constitutional under **Art. 338**.
NCST chair: **Antar Singh Arya** (**Art. 338A**).

57.s: Which one of the following correctly indicates the latest host and the next planned host of the BIMSTEC Summit?
57.x: The 6th BIMSTEC Summit was held in Bangkok in 2025, and the next summit is planned in Bangladesh.
57.tq: Separate the completed host from the next planned host.
xs: The **6th BIMSTEC Summit** was held at **Bangkok** (**April 2025**) and the next is planned in **Bangladesh** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Thailand hosted it; Bangladesh is the chair for **2026**.
xa: 6th BIMSTEC theme: "**Prosperous, Resilient and Open**".
**SAARC's** last (**18th**) summit was at **Kathmandu, 2014**; it is now suspended.
**Mekong Ganga Cooperation** was launched at **Vientiane (Laos), 2000**.

57.s:
Consider the following statements about the 17th BRICS Summit:
1. It was held at Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, in July 2025.
2. It was chaired by Xi Jinping.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
57.x: Statement 1 is correct: the 17th BRICS Summit was held at Rio de Janeiro in July 2025. Statement 2 is wrong: it was chaired by Brazil's Lula da Silva, not Xi Jinping. Hence 1 only; B, C and D are wrong.
57.tq: Host country's leader chairs the summit: Brazil hosted, so Lula chaired.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — so option **(1) 1 only** is the answer.
Statement 1 is correct: the **17th BRICS** Summit was at **Rio de Janeiro**, Brazil, in **July 2025**.
Statement 2 is wrong: it was chaired by Brazil's **Lula da Silva**, not Xi Jinping.
xa: Rio adopted the **Leaders' Framework Declaration on Climate Finance**.
At Rio, India explained BRICS as "**Building Resilience and Innovation for Cooperation and Sustainability**".
The **18th BRICS** was in **New Delhi** (**12-13 Sep 2026**).

57.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the 18th BRICS Summit:
1. It was held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi.
2. It was held on 12–13 September 2026.
3. India handed over the BRICS chair to China for 2027.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
57.x: All three statements are correct. The 18th BRICS Summit was held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, on 12–13 September 2026, and the chair was to pass from India to China for 2027.
57.tq: Statement combination testing venue, date and chair handover.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is the answer.
Statements 1 and 2: the **18th BRICS** Summit was at **Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi**, on **12-13 Sep 2026**.
Statement 3: India handed the chair to **China** for **2027**.
xa: Theme: "**Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability**".
Outcome: the **New Delhi Declaration**, adopted unanimously.
⚠ **18th G20** = New Delhi **2023**; **18th BRICS** = New Delhi **2026** — both at **Bharat Mandapam**.

57.s: The theme of the 18th BRICS Summit held in New Delhi was:
o: One Earth, One Family, One Future
Upholding the Shanghai Spirit: SCO on the Move
Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability
57.x: The theme of the 18th BRICS Summit was “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability.”
57.tq: Exact-theme recall with themes of other groupings as traps.
xs: The **18th BRICS** theme was "**Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability**" — so option **(4)** is correct.
"**One Earth, One Family, One Future**" = **G20 2023**; "**Upholding the Shanghai Spirit**" = **SCO 2025**; "**Solidarity, Equality, and Sustainability**" = **G20 2025**.
xa: The theme recasts the **BRICS** acronym, as Modi did at Rio.
The summit was at **Bharat Mandapam**, **12-13 Sep 2026**.
India → **China (2027)** chair handover.

57.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
57.x: The 20th G20 Summit was held in Johannesburg, South Africa, in November 2025. It was the first G20 Summit held on African soil.
57.tq: Start from the sure venue-edition pair and eliminate swapped summit locations.
xs: The **20th G20** Summit was held at **Johannesburg, South Africa** (Nov 2025) — so option **(1)** is correct.
**New Delhi** hosted the **18th G20** (**2023**); **Tianjin** hosted **SCO 2025**; **Évian** hosted the **52nd G7**.
xa: It was the **first G20 on African soil**.
Outcome: the **Johannesburg Leaders' Declaration**, adopted unusually early.
The **African Union** membership was fully operationalised at Johannesburg.

57.s: The theme of the 20th G20 Summit hosted by South Africa in 2025 was associated with which of the following?
o: Working Together to Address Major International Challenges
Solidarity, Equality, and Sustainability; the spirit of Ubuntu
Inclusivity and Sustainability; ASEAN rotational chairmanship
57.x: The 20th G20 Summit adopted the theme “Solidarity, Equality, and Sustainability”, reflecting the philosophy of Ubuntu, or “I am because we are.”
57.tq: Theme-and-host association using exact official wording.
xs: The **20th G20** theme was "**Solidarity, Equality, and Sustainability**", in the spirit of **Ubuntu** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Ubuntu means "**I am because we are**".
"**Prosperous, Resilient and Open**" = **BIMSTEC**; "**Working Together...**" = **52nd G7**; "**Inclusivity and Sustainability**" = **20th EAS**.
xa: The Johannesburg Declaration set up a **Cost of Capital Commission**.
It had the **first standalone debt declaration** since COVID.
The U.S. skipped **G20 2025**.

57.s: The 25th Summit of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation was held at:
57.x: The 25th SCO Summit was held in Tianjin, China, on 31 August–1 September 2025. China hosted the SCO Summit for the fifth time.
57.tq: Edition-to-venue matching with confusable SCO and ASEAN venues.
xs: The **25th SCO** Summit was held at **Tianjin, China** (**31 Aug-1 Sep 2025**) — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Bishkek** hosted the **26th SCO** (2026); **Ankara** the **36th NATO**; **Kuala Lumpur** the **20th EAS**.
xa: China hosted the SCO for the **5th** time.
Theme: "**Upholding the Shanghai Spirit: SCO on the Move**".
The **Tianjin Declaration** endorsed an **SCO development bank**.

57.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the 26th SCO Summit:
1. It is scheduled to be held in Bishkek.
2. Kyrgyzstan is the host country.
3. Its theme refers to 25 years of the SCO.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
57.x: All three statements are correct. The 26th SCO Summit is scheduled at Bishkek in Kyrgyzstan in 2026, with the theme “25 Years of SCO: Together for Sustainable Peace, Development and Prosperity.”
57.tq: Combine venue, host and theme clues without confusing the 25th and 26th editions.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is the answer.
Statements 1 and 2: the **26th SCO** is at **Bishkek**, hosted by the **Kyrgyz Republic** (**31 Aug-1 Sep 2026**).
Statement 3: theme "**25 Years of SCO**: Together for Sustainable Peace, Development and Prosperity".
xa: The **Bishkek Declaration** was one of **28 documents** adopted.
It approved an **SCO-CSTO-CIS roadmap**.
Next chair: **Pakistan (2026-27)**, summit at **Islamabad**.

57.s: Which of the following statements about the 52nd G7 Summit is correct?
o: Its chair was Lula da Silva of Brazil.
The United States hosted the 52nd G7 Summit in 2026.
Its theme was “Working Together to Address Major International Challenges”.
It was held in Kananaskis, Canada, in June 2026.
57.x: The 52nd G7 Summit was held in Évian-les-Bains, France, under Emmanuel Macron, with the theme “Working Together to Address Major International Challenges.”
57.tq: Find the one precisely matched statement among year, venue and chair swaps.
xs: The **52nd G7** theme was "**Working Together to Address Major International Challenges**" — so option **(3)** is correct.
It was hosted by **Emmanuel Macron** at **Évian-les-Bains, France** (June 2026); **Lula** chaired BRICS Rio; **Kananaskis** hosted the **51st** (2025).
The **U.S.** hosts the **53rd G7** in **2027**, not the 52nd.
xa: Évian adopted a declaration on **Securing Supply Chains for Critical Minerals** (via **PGII**).
It also covered debt relief, the **Strait of Hormuz**, cancer research and minors' online safety.
Russia was admitted in **1998** (G8) and suspended in **2014** after Crimea.

57.s: The 22nd ASEAN–India Summit was held in which manner and under whose chair?
o: Physically in Bangkok under Thailand’s chair
Virtually under China’s chair as part of the SCO Summit
Physically in New Delhi under India’s chair
Virtually under Malaysia’s chair as part of the 47th ASEAN Summit
57.x: The 22nd ASEAN–India Summit was held virtually under Malaysia’s chair and formed part of the 47th ASEAN Summit in Kuala Lumpur in October 2025.
57.tq: Split the option into format, chair and institutional setting before choosing.
xs: The **22nd ASEAN-India** Summit was held **virtually** under **Malaysia's** chair, as part of the **47th ASEAN Summit** in **Kuala Lumpur** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It was not a physical summit in Bangkok or New Delhi, nor part of an SCO meeting.
xa: Outcomes: **2026** = **ASEAN-India Year of Maritime Cooperation**.
An ASEAN-India Comprehensive Strategic Partnership plan **2026-2030**.
A call for early **AITIGA** review.

57.s: The 20th East Asia Summit was held in 2025 at:
57.x: The 20th East Asia Summit was held in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, in 2025. The EAS was founded in 2005 in Kuala Lumpur.
57.tq: Venue-year association with the founding-place clue.
xs: The **20th East Asia Summit** was held at **Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia** (2025) — so option **(2)** is correct.
Its theme was "**Inclusivity and Sustainability**".
xa: The EAS was founded in **2005** at Kuala Lumpur.
It now has **19** members (**11 ASEAN + 8 partners**).
Outcome: the **Kuala Lumpur Declaration** on peace and stability in the Indo-Pacific.

57.s: Which of the following statements regarding the East Asia Summit is correct?
o: Its chair rotates annually among G20 members.
It was founded in 2015 at Bangkok.
Its chair is permanently held by Malaysia.
57.x: The 2025 East Asia Summit had the theme “Inclusivity and Sustainability”. Its chair rotates annually among ASEAN members, and it was founded in 2005.
57.tq: Reject permanent-chair and wrong-founding-year traps.
xs: The **2025 EAS** theme was "**Inclusivity and Sustainability**" — so option **(4)** is correct.
Its chair rotates annually among **ASEAN** members (not G20, not permanently Malaysia); it was founded in **2005** at **Kuala Lumpur**, not 2015 at Bangkok.
xa: The **20th EAS** was in **Kuala Lumpur**.
EAS has **19** members: **11 ASEAN + 8 partners**.
Philippines hosts the EAS FMs (**16th**, **Manila**) in 2026.

57.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: G7 2026 — Working Together to Address Major International Challenges
G20 2023 — One Earth, One Family, One Future
SCO 2025 — Together for Sustainable Peace, Development and Prosperity
57.x: The 2025 SCO theme was “Upholding the Shanghai Spirit: SCO on the Move.” “Together for Sustainable Peace, Development and Prosperity” was the theme of the 2026 SCO Summit.
57.tq: Find the swapped theme between successive editions of the same organisation.
xs: **SCO 2025 — Together for Sustainable Peace, Development and Prosperity** is the wrong pair — so option **(4)** is the answer.
The **SCO 2025** (Tianjin) theme was "**Upholding the Shanghai Spirit: SCO on the Move**"; the quoted words belong to **SCO 2026** (Bishkek).
The rest are right: **G7 2026** "Working Together..."; **G20 2023** "One Earth, One Family, One Future"; **G20 2025** "Solidarity, Equality, and Sustainability".
xa: The 2026 SCO theme begins "**25 Years of SCO**".
**6th BIMSTEC** theme: "**Prosperous, Resilient and Open**".
**20th EAS** theme: "**Inclusivity and Sustainability**".

57.s: Which of the following correctly represents the planned succession of the SCO chair mentioned for the relevant summit cycle?
57.x: The stated succession was China, followed by Kyrgyzstan in 2026 and Pakistan for 2026–27, with the summit planned at Islamabad.
57.tq: Sequence recall using chair handover rather than summit venue.
xs: The SCO chair passes **China → Kyrgyzstan (2026) → Pakistan (2026-27)** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The Pakistan-chaired summit is planned at **Islamabad**.
xa: "**Pakistan now chairs SCO**" is listed as current relevance.
**SCO Tourism and Cultural Capital 2026-27**: **Lahore**.
⚠ BRICS chair: India (2026) → **China (2027)** — do not confuse with the SCO order.

57.s: The 52nd G7 Summit (June 2026) was held at:
57.x: The 52nd G7 Summit was held at Evian-les-Bains, France, hosted by Emmanuel Macron; the U.S. hosts the 53rd in 2027. Kananaskis, Canada hosted the 51st (2025). Hiroshima and Apulia hosted earlier G7 summits.
57.tq: Exam angle: match the edition with the city. 51st Kananaskis, 52nd Evian.
xs: The **52nd G7** (June 2026) was held at **Evian-les-Bains, France**, hosted by **Emmanuel Macron** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Kananaskis, Canada** hosted the **51st G7** (June 2025).
xa: The **U.S.** hosts the **53rd G7** in **2027**.
⚠ **G7 51st** = Kananaskis; **52nd** = Évian.
**One Health Summit 2026** was at **Lyon, France** under the G7 Presidency.

57.s: The theme of the 6th BIMSTEC Summit held at Bangkok in April 2025 was:
o: Working Together to Address Major International Challenges
57.x: The 6th BIMSTEC Summit (Bangkok, Thailand, April 2025) had the theme 'Prosperous, Resilient and Open' (PYQ); the next summit is planned in Bangladesh. 'Inclusivity and Sustainability' was the 20th EAS theme, 'Solidarity, Equality, and Sustainability' the G20 Johannesburg theme, and 'Working Together...' the 52nd G7 theme.
57.tq: BIMSTEC Bangkok = PRO: Prosperous, Resilient, Open.
xs: The **6th BIMSTEC** (Bangkok, **April 2025**) theme was "**Prosperous, Resilient and Open**" — so option **(3)** is correct.
"**Inclusivity and Sustainability**" = **20th EAS**; "**Solidarity, Equality, and Sustainability**" = **G20 Johannesburg**; "**Working Together...**" = **52nd G7**.
xa: The next BIMSTEC summit is planned in **Bangladesh** (chair **2026**).
Thailand was the host.
Exam angle: match the **edition number** with the city, not just the country.

57.s: India holds the chair of BRICS in which year in the stated rotation?
57.x: India is the BRICS chair in 2026. China is scheduled to chair BRICS in 2027.
57.tq: Separate the current chair from the next chair in a rotation question.
xs: India chairs **BRICS** in **2026** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**China** chairs BRICS in **2027**; **2025** was Brazil (Rio).
xa: India hosted the **18th BRICS**, New Delhi, **12-13 Sep 2026**.
BRICS 2026 meetings: **Puri** (disaster risk), **Bengaluru** (space), **Varanasi** (culture), **Jaipur** (industry, PV).
The **16th BRICS NSA meeting** (chair **Ajit Doval**) in New Delhi ended with no joint statement.

57.s: India explained BRICS at Rio as “Building Resilience and Innovation for Cooperation and Sustainability”. What does this phrase represent?
o: The motto of the SCO Bishkek Summit
The name of the BRICS development bank
The official title of the Johannesburg Declaration
The expanded meaning of BRICS presented by India
57.x: At Rio, India explained BRICS as “Building Resilience and Innovation for Cooperation and Sustainability” - an expanded reading of the acronym BRICS.
57.tq: Recognise a descriptive expansion as an institutional formulation, not a declaration or body.
xs: "**Building Resilience and Innovation for Cooperation and Sustainability**" is India's **expanded meaning of BRICS**, given at **Rio** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It is not an SCO motto, a bank's name or a G20 declaration title.
xa: The **18th BRICS** theme recast it as "**Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability**".
**BRIC** was coined in **2001** by **Jim O'Neill**.
BRICS chair: India (**2026**) → **China (2027)**.

57.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (BRICS meeting)
a. 16th NSA meeting
b. Disaster Risk Reduction meeting
c. Space agencies meeting
 d. Cultural Working Group
List-II (Indian city)
i. Varanasi
ii. Puri
iii. Bengaluru
iv. New Delhi
57.x: The 16th NSA meeting was at New Delhi, Disaster Risk Reduction at Puri, space agencies at Bengaluru and the Cultural Working Group at Varanasi.
57.tq: Start from the sure venue pairs and verify that no List-II item is repeated.
xs: The correct match is **a–iv, b–ii, c–iii, d–i** — option **(1)**.
**16th NSA** meeting → **New Delhi**; **Disaster Risk Reduction** (first in-person) → **Puri**.
**Space agencies** (ISRO) → **Bengaluru**; **Cultural Working Group** → **Varanasi**.
xa: BRICS **Industry Ministers** met at **Jaipur** (PV Action Plan).
The NSA meeting was chaired by **Ajit Doval** and had no joint statement.
⚠ **Puri** = disaster risk; **Bengaluru** = space; **Varanasi** = culture; **Jaipur** = industry.

57.s: Which city has been designated as the SCO Tourism and Cultural Capital for 2026–27?
57.x: Lahore has been designated the SCO Tourism and Cultural Capital for 2026–27.
57.tq: Distinguish the cultural capital from the city hosting the SCO summit.
xs: **Lahore** is the **SCO Tourism and Cultural Capital 2026-27** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Bishkek** hosts the **26th SCO** summit; **Tianjin** hosted the **25th**; **Islamabad** is the planned summit venue under Pakistan's chair.
xa: SCO chair: China → Kyrgyzstan (**2026**) → **Pakistan (2026-27)**.
The **Bishkek Declaration** condemned **U.S.-Israel attacks on Iran** and terrorism "in all forms".
The **Tianjin Declaration** condemned the **Pahalgam** and **Jaffer Express** attacks.

57.s: Which statement regarding the 2026 G20 Summit is correct?
o: It was held under the South African presidency in Johannesburg.
It was held under the Indian presidency in New Delhi.
It was held under the Chinese presidency in Beijing.
It falls under the United States presidency, with venue and date not specified here.
57.x: The 2026 G20 Summit is under the United States presidency; the venue and date were not specified in the stated information.
57.tq: Avoid adding an unstated venue or date to a presidency fact.
xs: The **2026 G20** is under the **US presidency**; its venue and date are not given in the notes — so option **(4)** is correct.
**South Africa** held the **2025** presidency (Johannesburg); **India** held it in **2023** (New Delhi).
xa: The **20th G20** (Johannesburg) was the **first G20 on African soil**.
G20 presidency rotates annually among **five** regional groups.
**Troika** = past + present + next presidencies.

57.s: Which of the following was NOT an outcome associated with the 22nd ASEAN–India Summit?
o: Call for an early review of AITIGA
Adoption of the Shanghai Spirit as the guiding principle
ASEAN–India Comprehensive Strategic Partnership plan for 2026–2030
Declaration of 2026 as the ASEAN–India Year of Maritime Cooperation
57.x: The Shanghai Spirit was associated with the 25th SCO Summit. The ASEAN–India Summit outcomes included the maritime cooperation year, the 2026–2030 partnership plan and an early AITIGA review.
57.tq: Find the outcome belonging to another regional grouping.
xs: **Adoption of the Shanghai Spirit** is not an ASEAN-India outcome — so option **(2)** is the answer.
"**Shanghai Spirit**" was the theme of the **25th SCO** (Tianjin, 2025).
The real **22nd ASEAN-India** outcomes: **2026** Year of Maritime Cooperation, a **2026-2030** partnership plan and an early **AITIGA** review.
xa: The 22nd ASEAN-India Summit was held **virtually** under **Malaysia**.
It was part of the **47th ASEAN Summit, Kuala Lumpur**.
**Timor-Leste** is ASEAN's **11th** member (first summit **Oct 2025**).

57.s: The New Delhi Declaration adopted at the BRICS Summit in September 2026 was significant because it was:
o: the first BRICS declaration to endorse an SCO development bank
the first BRICS declaration to admit new members
the first BRICS declaration since 2022 with no reference to Ukraine
the first BRICS declaration to establish a common currency
57.x: The New Delhi Declaration was unanimously adopted and was the first BRICS declaration since 2022 that contained no reference to Ukraine.
57.tq: Use the precise distinguishing feature rather than the broader summit name.
xs: The **New Delhi Declaration** (**Sep 2026**) was the **first BRICS declaration since 2022 with no reference to Ukraine** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **SCO development bank** was endorsed by the SCO **Tianjin** Declaration, not BRICS.
xa: It was adopted **unanimously**; it backs **UNSC reform** (China, Russia back India, Brazil).
It rejects unilateral sanctions and carbon tariffs (**CBAM**) and has a **Pahalgam** paragraph.
**NIMHANS** will coordinate the BRICS mental-health centres.

57.s: Which institution has been designated to coordinate the BRICS mental-health centres under the New Delhi Declaration of 2026?
o: National Institute of Mental Health, Brazil
57.x: NIMHANS will coordinate the BRICS mental-health centres under the New Delhi Declaration.
57.tq: Test the institution associated with a specific initiative.
xs: **NIMHANS** will coordinate the **BRICS mental-health centres** under the **New Delhi Declaration** — so option **(1)** is correct (**16 Sep 2026**).
The New Delhi Declaration was adopted at the **18th BRICS** Summit, chaired by **India**.
xa: The declaration welcomed the **BRICS Photovoltaic Industry Action Plan** (adopted at **Jaipur**).
It also backs **IMF/WB reform**.
It was the first BRICS declaration since **2022** with no reference to Ukraine.

57.s: The BRICS Photovoltaic Industry Action Plan was adopted at which place in August 2026?
57.x: The BRICS Photovoltaic Industry Action Plan was adopted at Jaipur in August 2026 and was welcomed at the 18th BRICS Summit.
57.tq: Separate the venue of an initiative from the venue of the main summit.

It set up the **Belém Action Mechanism** on just transition and **60 GGA indicators**.

India **withdrew its bid** for **COP33 (2028)**.

**COP30** (Belém) was the first COP in the **Amazon**.

An FAO treaty on plant genetic resources

Ethiopia, Saudi Arabia, Indonesia and the United Arab Emirates

**NATO** has **32** members: **Finland (31st)** in **2023**, **Sweden (32nd)** in **2024**.

63.s: Which of the following correctly describes the composition of the G20 as given in the current grouping?

19 countries and only the African Union
18 countries, the European Union and ASEAN

63.s:

Statement 2 is correct: APEC has **21 economies** and its Secretariat is in **Singapore**.
Statement 3 is correct: the **APEC 2025** summit was at **Gyeongju, South Korea**.

Nuclear disarmament and strategic arms reduction

xs: **Pax Silica** is a **U.S.-led** initiative on **critical minerals, semiconductor and AI supply chains** — so option **(1)** is correct.

63.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

63.tq: Discriminate among conventions dealing with closely related environmental and trade subjects.
xs: **Vienna Convention, 1985 — ozone layer protection** is correctly matched — option **(1)**.
**Mercury** is covered by the **Minamata Convention** (**2013**), so option (2) is wrong.
The **Basel Convention** governs transboundary **hazardous waste**; the **Windsor Framework** is about **Northern Ireland** trade, not aviation.
xa: The **Montreal Protocol** (**1987**) on ozone-depleting substances is universally ratified (**197**).

xs: The **Hague Conventions** (HCCH) deal with **private international law** — so option **(4)** is correct.

Civil aviation is the **Chicago Convention** (**1944**); monetary cooperation is the **IMF**.
xa: ⚠ **Hague** = private international law; **Chicago** = civil aviation; **Basel** = hazardous waste.
The **Windsor Framework** (**2023**) sets UK-EU post-Brexit trade rules for **Northern Ireland**.
The **Water Convention** (**Helsinki 1992**) covers transboundary rivers and lakes.

xs: The **Basel Convention (1989)** governs transboundary **hazardous waste** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Minamata** (**2013**) is about **mercury**; **Stockholm** (**2001**) is about **POPs**.
xa: Basel has a **plastic-waste amendment** and **stronger e-waste** rules.
Stockholm lists **34** chemicals, recently **Chlorpyrifos** and **PFAS**.
Minamata: **dental amalgam** to be phased out by **2034**.

63.s: The Stockholm Convention of 2001 primarily concerns:
63.x: The Stockholm Convention deals with persistent organic pollutants. The listed framework covers 34 chemicals, including recently noted substances such as chlorpyrifos and PFAS.

xs: The **Stockholm Convention (2001)** concerns **persistent organic pollutants (POPs)** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Child abduction is a **Hague** convention; Northern Ireland trade is the **Windsor Framework**; civil aviation is the **Chicago Convention**.
xa: It covers **34** chemicals, recently **Chlorpyrifos** and **PFAS**.
⚠ **Basel** = hazardous waste; **Stockholm** = POPs; **Minamata** = mercury; **Vienna/Montreal** = ozone.
**Basel** (**1989**) has a **plastic-waste amendment**.

63.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the Minamata Convention?
o: Mercury; dental amalgam to be phased out by 2034

xs: The **Minamata Convention (2013)** is about **mercury**, with **dental amalgam** to be phased out by **2034** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**POPs/34 chemicals** = **Stockholm**; ozone/Montreal Protocol = **Vienna**; hazardous waste/plastic amendment = **Basel**.
xa: **Stockholm** (**2001**): recently added **Chlorpyrifos** and **PFAS**.
The **Montreal Protocol** is universally ratified (**197**).
**Basel** (**1989**) has stronger **e-waste** rules.

The global trade in hazardous chemicals
The admission of new NATO members

Civil aviation = **Chicago Convention** (**1944**); NATO's newest members are **Finland** and **Sweden**.

B. Chicago Convention
C. Stockholm Convention
D. Basel Convention
63.x: The correct sequence is Chicago Convention (1944), Basel Convention (1989), Stockholm Convention (2001), and Minamata Convention (2013).

63.s:
Consider the following statements about the Water Convention:

2. It entered into force in 1996.
3. It concerns transboundary rivers and lakes.

Statement 4: **Bangladesh** is the **first South Asian party**.

63.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?

Convention on Supplementary Compensation — India became a party in 2016
Convention on Supplementary Compensation — adopted in 1997; entered into force in 2015
Convention on Nuclear Safety — adopted in 1994; entered into force in 1996

xa: The **SHANTI Act 2025** caps nuclear liability at **300 million SDRs** (about **₹3,900 crore**).

63.s: With reference to the five United Nations outer-space treaties, which one of the following is correct regarding India?
o: India has ratified all five but signed only four.
India has signed and ratified all five.
India has signed all five and ratified four, but not the Moon Agreement of 1979.
India has neither signed nor ratified the Moon Agreement but has ratified only three others.
63.x: India has signed all five UN outer-space treaties and ratified four. The exception is the 1979 Moon Agreement, which India has not ratified.

63.s: Which one of the following statements about the Montreal Protocol is correct?
o: It was replaced by the Chicago Convention in 2026.

69.s: Which one of the following correctly describes India's Act East Policy?

69.s: The first visit of an Indian Defence Minister to Colombo in nearly four decades was undertaken by whom?

**BrahMos-NG**: **Philippines** = first export customer.

69.s:

69.s: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the IPEF and SCO?

69.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Balendra (Balen) Shah:
1. He was sworn in as Prime Minister of Nepal in March 2026.
2. At 35, he became Nepal's youngest Prime Minister.
3. His Rastriya Swatantra Party formed a coalition government after failing to win a majority.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
69.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: he was sworn in on 27 Mar 2026, aged 35, the youngest PM. Statement 3 is wrong: the RSP won a majority (about two-thirds) on 5 Mar 2026. So 1 and 2 only.
69.tq: Balen Shah: RSP two-thirds majority, youngest (35), first of Madhesh descent.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — so option **(1) 1 and 2 only** is correct.
Statement 1: **Balen Shah** was sworn in as Nepal's PM on **27 Mar 2026** — correct.
Statement 2: at **35** he is Nepal's **youngest PM** — correct.
Statement 3 is wrong: the **RSP** won a **majority** (~**two-thirds**) on **5 Mar 2026**, not a coalition.
xa: He is also the **first PM of Madhesh descent**.
The change followed **Gen Z protests** (**Sep 2025**) that toppled **K.P. Sharma Oli**.
⚠ **Sushila Karki** = interim PM; **Balen Shah** = elected PM.

69.s:

Nepal claimed **Kalapani-Limpiyadhura** (**Mar 2026**).

Statements 3-4: **26 Rafale-M** (Navy, **Apr 2025**); **114 Rafale (MRFA)** AoN on **12 Feb 2026** — correct.

**France** has offered a **Make-in-India** model for the MRFA (Jun 2026).

69.s:

69.x: The S-400 Triumf is a Russian-origin air-defence system, is referred to as ‘Sudarshan Chakra’, and has a stated range of 400 km.
69.tq: Combine related platform, alias and numerical facts in a coded statement question.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
The **S-400 Triumf** is **Russian**, called "**Sudarshan Chakra**", with a **400 km** range.
xa: It was used in **Op Sindoor** — its **first** use in high-intensity combat.

69.s: The MQ-9B Sea Guardian is best described as which of the following?

xs: The **MQ-9B Sea Guardian** is a **U.S.-origin HALE drone** (**General Atomics**) — so option **(3)** is correct.
France supplies the **Rafale** fighter; Israel's **Iron Dome** is the missile shield; Italy's **WASS** supplies heavyweight torpedoes.

Other U.S. buys: **6 more P-8I** (AoN Feb 2026) and the **Javelin** ATGM (LOA Aug 2026).
**Tata (TASL)** and Javelin signed a co-production MoU.

69.s:

69.x: Statement 1 is correct: Iron Dome (Israel) is the model. Statement 2 is wrong: the multi-layer shield is targeted by 2035, not 2030. So 1 only.
69.tq: Sudarshan Chakra shield = 2035, modelled on Israel's Iron Dome.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — so option **(1) 1 only** is correct.

Statement 2 is wrong: the multi-layer shield is targeted by **2035**, not 2030.

The S-400 has a **400 km** range and was used in **Op Sindoor**.
India's nuclear doctrine (**2003**): **No First Use**, credible minimum deterrence.

69.s:

xs: All four statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4** is correct.

The U.S. **MQ-9B Sea Guardian** lease: **2** drones, **30 months**, **₹1,943 crore**.
India signed the **Javelin** LOA (**Aug 2026**).

69.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: CQB carbines — Bharat Forge and PLR
Heavyweight torpedoes for Kalvari submarines — Italy (WASS)
Kalvari submarines — Israel and Rafael Advanced Defense Systems
69.x: Kalvari-class Scorpene submarines are based on French Naval Group technology and are built at MDL. The other three pairings are correct.

Israel's link in the notes is **Iron Dome**, the model for Mission Sudarshan Chakra.

69.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Kalvari-class submarines is correct?
o: They are entirely of Russian design and were built at Cochin Shipyard.
They comprise six P-75 submarines, with INS Vaghsheer being the last one delivered in 2025.
They comprise four submarines, with INS Vaghsheer delivered in 2024.
They comprise eight submarines, with INS Vaghsheer delivered in 2026.
69.x: The P-75 programme comprises six Kalvari-class Scorpene submarines. INS Vaghsheer was the last submarine and was delivered in 2025.

xs: The **Kalvari** class = **six P-75** submarines; the last, **INS Vaghsheer**, came in **2025** — so option **(2)** is correct.
They are **French** (Naval Group) design built at **MDL, Mumbai** — not Russian or Cochin-built.
xa: Their **heavyweight torpedoes** come from **Italy** (**WASS**), contract **Jan 2026**.
The Kalvari subs are **Scorpene**-class boats.
**Nipun**, a Diving Support Vessel built by **Hindustan Shipyard Ltd**, was delivered at **Visakhapatnam** (Aug 2026).

69.s: RELOS, signed between India and Russia in February 2025 and operationalised in June 2026, relates to:
69.x: RELOS is the India–Russia logistics pact, signed in February 2025 and operationalised in June 2026.

xs: **RELOS** is the India-**Russia** **logistics pact**, signed **Feb 2025** and operationalised **Jun 2026** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was finalised at the **23rd Annual Summit** (Dec 2025).
xa: That summit set a **$100 bn** trade target by **2030**.
The India-US logistics pact is **LEMOA (2016)**.
Heavy reliance on **Russian platforms** limits India's defence diversification.

69.s: The UNICORN stealth naval mast represents the first India–Japan co-manufacturing agreement in the field of:
69.x: UNICORN is a stealth naval mast and marks the first India–Japan co-manufacturing agreement in this area.
69.tq: Link a named defence technology with its specific domain and partner country.
xs: **UNICORN** is a **stealth naval mast** — the first India-Japan co-manufacturing agreement, in **naval systems** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It was signed in **Jul 2026**.
xa: India-Japan signed a **maritime security arrangement** (**Aug 2026**).
**JIMEX** is the India-Japan naval exercise.
The **16th India-Japan Annual Summit** adopted a Joint Declaration on **Economic Security**.

69.s: With reference to BrahMos, which country is its first export customer, and where is the new BrahMos-NG plant located?

69.tq: BrahMos: Philippines first buyer; NG plant Lucknow.
xs: **BrahMos-NG**: the **Philippines** is the **first export customer**, and the new plant is in **Lucknow** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Option (2) is wrong on both; option (3) has the wrong customer; option (4) has the wrong plant.
xa: The Lucknow plant is in the **Defence Corridor**.
India-**Philippines** became **Strategic Partners** (**Aug 2025**).
**MILAN 2026** saw first-time ships from the **Philippines**, Germany and UAE.

69.s: The Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Project, including Sittwe port, is associated with:
69.x: The Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Project is located in Myanmar and includes the Sittwe port component.

xs: The **Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit** project (**Sittwe** port) is in **Myanmar** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It eases the load on the **Siliguri Corridor**.
**Agalega** = Mauritius; **Punatsangchhu-I** / **Mangdechhu** = Bhutan; **MoD building** = Maldives.

Operation **Brahma** = **Myanmar** earthquake relief (2025).
**Min Aung Hlaing** became Myanmar's President (**10 Apr 2026**).

69.s:

3. The project is intended to improve regional connectivity.

69.x: The highway is 1,360 km long, connects India through Myanmar to Thailand, and is a regional connectivity project.

xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.

It is a regional connectivity project, still **under way**.

Thailand became a **Strategic Partner** in **2025**.

69.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?

69.s: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes Punatsangchhu-I from Mangdechhu?
o: Punatsangchhu-I is 1,200 MW and work resumed in April 2026, whereas Mangdechhu is 720 MW and was commissioned in 2019.
Punatsangchhu-I is 720 MW and was commissioned in 2019, whereas Mangdechhu is 1,200 MW and resumed work in 2026.

xs: **Punatsangchhu-I** is **1,200 MW** (work **resumed Apr 2026**), while **Mangdechhu** is **720 MW** (commissioned **2019**) — so option **(1)** is correct.

**Agalega** (Mauritius) is India's forward naval facility.
**Chabahar** (Iran) was leased in **2024**.

69.s: Which of the following statements regarding India’s response to the 2026 West Asia crisis is correct?
o: India suspended all naval activity in the Indian Ocean.

India transferred the Chabahar terminal to the United States.

**Sindhu** evacuated Indians from **Iran / West Asia**.
The West Asia war began on **28 Feb 2026**; a **US-Iran MoU** followed in **Jun 2026**.

69.s: The principal criticism of the GE F414 arrangement is that:

69.s: Heavy reliance on Russian defence platforms has been criticised mainly because it:
o: Limits diversification of India’s defence suppliers
Eliminates the need for indigenous production
Prevents India from operating naval platforms
Makes all Indian systems exclusively French
69.x: Dependence on Russian platforms is criticised because it limits diversification of India’s defence procurement sources.

xs: Heavy reliance on **Russian platforms** is criticised because it **limits diversification** of India's defence suppliers — so option **(1)** is correct.
Russian-origin systems include the **S-400 Triumf** (**400 km** range).
xa: **RELOS**, the India-Russia logistics pact, was signed in **Feb 2025** and operationalised in **Jun 2026**.
India's other suppliers: **France** (Rafale, Scorpene), **U.S.** (P-8I, MQ-9B, Javelin), **Italy** (WASS torpedoes), **Israel** (Iron Dome model).
The **GE F414** deal keeps the single-crystal blade process with the US.

69.s:

xs: **Nipun**, the **2nd Diving Support Vessel**, was built by **Hindustan Shipyard Ltd** — so option **(1)** is correct.

**Mazagon Dock (MDL)** built the **Kalvari** (Scorpene) submarines, not Nipun.

**Visakhapatnam** hosted **MILAN 2026**, **IFR 2026** and the **IONS Conclave** (Feb 2026).
The last Kalvari-class sub, **INS Vaghsheer**, came in **2025**.

75.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the radar configuration of NISAR?

Both L-band and S-band supplied by ISRO
75.x: NISAR carries dual radar: NASA provides the L-band system and ISRO provides the S-band system.

xs: **NISAR** carries **L-band** radar from **NASA** and **S-band** radar from **ISRO** — so option **(1)** is correct.

xa: NISAR was launched on **30 Jul 2025** by **GSLV-F16** from **Sriharikota**.

NISAR is the **first ISRO-NASA joint satellite**.

o: Solar corona, lunar craters and exoplanets
Only cloud formation and cyclone naming
Navigation signals, broadband and satellite docking
75.x: NISAR observes glaciers, earthquakes, land subsidence and biomass, among other Earth-system features.

xs: NISAR's objectives cover **glaciers**, **earthquakes**, **subsidence** and **biomass** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The full list: land deformation (earthquakes, landslides, subsidence), **ice sheets and glaciers**, ecosystems/biomass, **disasters**.
The **solar corona** is studied by ESA's **Proba-3**, not NISAR.
xa: NISAR = NASA **L-band** + ISRO **S-band** SAR.
It scans nearly all Earth every **12 days**.

75.s:

75.tq: Gaganyaan = 3-400-3; tracking help from ESA.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — so option **(3) 1 and 3 only** is correct.
Statement 1: **Gaganyaan** will take a crew of **3** to a **400 km** orbit for **3 days** — correct.
Statement 2 is wrong: **ESA**, not NASA, will give **ground-tracking** support.
Statement 3: **IADT-02** (**10 Apr 2026**) came ahead of the uncrewed **G1** flight — correct.

75.s:
Which of the following statements about NISAR is correct?

**NISAR** is the first ISRO-NASA joint satellite; **TRISHNA** is a planned ISRO-CNES thermal-infrared mission.

75.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Vikram-1 ('Aagaman')?
o: ISRO's first reusable launch vehicle; India became the second country after the US
