Statement 3: **New Delhi** was again the **most polluted capital**; **Pakistan** was the most polluted country.
xa: The report is published by **IQAir**, a **Swiss** body; only **14%** of cities met the WHO PM2.5 guideline of **5 µg/m³**.
⚠ Most polluted city: **2024 = Byrnihat (Meghalaya)**; **2025 = Loni (UP)**.
⚠ Sources differ on how many years in a row Delhi has been the most polluted capital: **Drishti IAS** says the **8th** straight year; **RAU's IAS** implies the **7th**.
**Delhi** is the city most often in the news for poor air (asked 2025).

82.s: According to the World Air Quality Report 2025, what proportion of cities met the WHO guideline of 5 µg/m³ for PM2.5?
82.x: Only 14% of cities met the WHO PM2.5 guideline of 5 µg/m³.
82.tq: Retain the exact percentage and the associated pollutant guideline.
xs: Only **14%** of cities met the **WHO PM2.5 guideline** of **5 µg/m³** — option **(2)**.
The figure is from the **World Air Quality Report 2025** of **IQAir, Switzerland**, released in **Mar 2026**.
xa: Most polluted country: **Pakistan**; most polluted city: **Loni (UP)**; **India 6th** (improved from 5th in 2024).
**New Delhi** was again the most polluted **capital**.
⚠ The **2024 edition** named **Byrnihat (Meghalaya)** the most polluted city.
In India, the **NCAP** (**2019**) covers **130 cities**, tracked on the **PRANA** portal.

82.s: The National Clean Air Programme (NCAP) was launched in 2019 by which ministry?
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
82.x: The NCAP was launched in 2019 by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC).
82.tq: Apply the ministry-ownership trap to an environmental programme.
xs: The **NCAP** was launched in **2019** by the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** — option **(1)**.
**Ministry of Power** is linked instead to **BEE**, which prepares the State Energy Efficiency Index.
xa: NCAP covers **130 cities** and its progress is tracked on the **PRANA** portal.
The **AQI** has **6 categories** based on **8 pollutants**: PM10, PM2.5, NO2, SO2, CO, O3, NH3 and Pb.
**Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan 2026** (5th edition) ranked the **130 NCAP cities**, announced on **7 Sep 2026** (Clean Air Day).
The **MoEFCC** rejects the methodology of the **EPI 2026**, which ranked India **176th of 177**.

82.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Clean Air Programme:
1. It covers 130 cities.
2. Its implementation is tracked through the PRANA portal.
3. The Air Quality Index under the programme is based on eight pollutants.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
82.x: The NCAP covers 130 cities, uses the PRANA portal for tracking, and the AQI is based on eight pollutants.
82.tq: Test a programme through its coverage, monitoring portal and measurement base.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: **NCAP** (launched **2019** by **MoEFCC**) covers **130 cities**.
Statement 2: its progress is tracked on the **PRANA** portal.
Statement 3: the **AQI** uses **8 pollutants** — PM10, PM2.5, NO2, SO2, CO, O3, NH3 and Pb.
xa: ⚠ **AQI** = **6** categories, **8** pollutants — do not swap the two numbers.
**Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan 2026** was the **5th edition**, covering the 130 NCAP cities.
Its winners: **Lucknow** (million-plus), **Rourkela** (3-10 lakh, **Guntur joint 2nd**), **Kalinga Nagar** (under 3 lakh).

82.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the eight pollutants used for the Air Quality Index mentioned in relation to NCAP?
82.x: The eight pollutants include PM10, PM2.5, NO2, SO2, CO, O3, NH3 and lead. Methane is not included in this list.
82.tq: Find the outsider by recalling the complete pollutant list.
xs: **Methane** is not one of the AQI pollutants — option **(2)**.
The **8 AQI pollutants** are **PM10, PM2.5, NO2, SO2, CO, O3 (ozone), NH3 (ammonia) and Pb (lead)**.
So **ammonia**, **PM2.5** and **ozone** are all included.
xa: The **AQI** has **6 categories**.
**NCAP**: launched **2019** by **MoEFCC**, covers **130 cities**, tracked on the **PRANA** portal.

82.s:
Consider the following statements about Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan 2026:
1. Lucknow topped the million-plus category.
2. Guntur topped the 3-10 lakh population category.
3. Kalinga Nagar topped the under-3-lakh category.

82.x: Statement 1 is correct: Lucknow topped the million-plus category. Statement 2 is wrong: Rourkela topped the 3-10 lakh category; Guntur was joint 2nd. Statement 3 is correct: Kalinga Nagar topped the under-3-lakh category. Statement 4 is correct: it was the 5th edition, covering 130 NCAP cities, on 7 Sep 2026 (Clean Air Day). So '1 and 3 only' is incomplete and options with 2 are wrong.
82.tq: AP trap: Guntur is joint SECOND; Rourkela is first in 3-10 lakh.
xs: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct — option **(2) 1, 3 and 4 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **Lucknow** topped the **million-plus** category.
Statement 2 wrong: **Rourkela** topped the **3-10 lakh** category; **Guntur** was only **joint 2nd**.
Statement 3 correct: **Kalinga Nagar** topped the **under 3 lakh** category.
Statement 4 correct: it was the **5th edition**, covering **130 NCAP cities**, on **7 Sep 2026**, **Clean Air Day**.
xa: **NCAP** was launched in **2019** by **MoEFCC** and is tracked on the **PRANA** portal.
AP angle: **Guntur 2nd** in Swachh Vayu 2026; **AP top** in SEEI 2024; **AP 2nd** in MISHTI.
The **AQI** has **6 categories** based on **8 pollutants**.

82.s: Which city is most frequently reported in connection with poor air quality in India?
82.x: Delhi is the city most often in the news for poor air quality (asked 2025). New Delhi was again the most polluted capital in the World Air Quality Report 2025.
82.tq: Distinguish the nationally prominent city from the State-specific pollution hotspot.
xs: **Delhi** is the city most often in the news for **poor air quality** (asked 2025) — option **(1)**.
In the **World Air Quality Report 2025**, **New Delhi** was again the **most polluted capital**.
xa: The most polluted **city** in 2025 was **Loni (UP)**; in **2024** it was **Byrnihat (Meghalaya)**.

Only **14%** of cities met the WHO PM2.5 guideline of **5 µg/m³**.

82.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Report)
a. Environmental Performance Index 2026
b. Climate Change Performance Index 2026
c. Climate Risk Index 2025
 d. State of India's Environment 2026 in Figures

List-II (Agency)
i. Germanwatch
 ii. Centre for Science and Environment and Down To Earth
 iii. Yale and Columbia Universities
 iv. Germanwatch, NewClimate Institute and CAN

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
82.x: EPI 2026 was released by Yale and Columbia; CCPI 2026 by Germanwatch, NewClimate Institute and CAN; Climate Risk Index 2025 by Germanwatch; and State of India's Environment by CSE and Down To Earth.
82.tq: Start from the sure agency-report pair and eliminate codes.
xs: Correct code: **a–iii, b–iv, c–i, d–ii** — option **(1)**.
**EPI 2026** → **Yale and Columbia Universities**; **CCPI 2026** → **Germanwatch, NewClimate Institute and CAN**.
**Climate Risk Index 2025** → **Germanwatch**; **State of India's Environment 2026 in Figures** → **CSE and Down To Earth**.
xa: ⚠ **Germanwatch** = CCPI + CRI; **Yale + Columbia** = EPI.
**EPI 2026**: India **176th of 177**, **Estonia** 1st; **CCPI 2026**: **India 23rd**, top 3 vacant, Denmark 4th.
**CRI 2025**: India **9th** worst hit (1995-2024) and **15th** for 2024 alone.
**State of India's Environment 2026**: **Goa** top state; PM2.5 deaths up **61%** in a decade.

82.s:
Consider the following statements about the Environmental Performance Index (EPI) 2026:
1. India ranked 176th of 177 countries.
2. Estonia ranked first.
3. The MoEFCC endorsed the methodology of the index.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
82.x: Statement 1 is correct: India was 176th of 177. Statement 2 is correct: Estonia was 1st. Statement 3 is wrong: the MoEFCC rejected the EPI methodology. So '1 only' is incomplete and the options containing 3 are wrong.
82.tq: India contests the EPI: MoEFCC rejected its method.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(3) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: India ranked **176th of 177** (score **22.46**) in **EPI 2026**.
Statement 2 correct: **Estonia** ranked **1st**.
Statement 3 wrong: the **MoEFCC rejects** the EPI methodology.
xa: **EPI** is prepared by **Yale and Columbia** Universities (Aug 2026).
⚠ Index contrast: **EPI 2026** (India 176/177) and **CCPI 2026** (India **23rd**) give opposite pictures; India contests the EPI.
**CCPI** is by **Germanwatch**, NewClimate Institute and CAN.

82.s:
With reference to the Climate Change Performance Index 2026, consider the following statements:
1. The top three positions were left vacant.
2. Denmark ranked fourth.
3. India ranked 23rd.
4. India's position declined by 13 places because of slow coal phase-down.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
82.x: All four statements correctly describe the CCPI 2026 results and India's decline attributed to slow coal phase-down.
82.tq: Use the vacant-top-three feature as an anchor before checking the remaining rankings.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**CCPI 2026** (Nov 2025): the **top 3** places were left **vacant** and **Denmark** was **4th**.
**India** was **23rd**, **down 13 places** because of its **slow coal phase-down**.
xa: The CCPI is published by **Germanwatch**, **NewClimate Institute** and **CAN**.
⚠ **Germanwatch** also publishes the **Climate Risk Index**: India **9th** worst hit (1995-2024).
Contrast: in **EPI 2026** (Yale and Columbia) India was **176th of 177**.

82.s: In the Climate Risk Index 2025, India was described as which of the following for the period 1995–2024?
82.x: For the period 1995–2024, India was ranked the ninth worst hit country in the Climate Risk Index 2025.
82.tq: Separate the long-period result from the single-year result.
xs: In the **Climate Risk Index 2025**, India was the **9th worst hit** country for **1995-2024** — option **(1)**.
**15th** is India's rank **for 2024 alone**, not the long-term period; **23rd** is India's **CCPI 2026** rank.
xa: The CRI is published by **Germanwatch** and was released at **COP30**.
The Hindu (24 Apr 2026) called India the **"9th most climate-vulnerable"** country.
⚠ **Germanwatch** = CRI + CCPI; **Yale + Columbia** = EPI.

82.s: Which state topped the State of India's Environment 2026 in Figures?
82.x: Goa was identified as the top state in the State of India's Environment 2026 in Figures.
82.tq: Use direct state-ranking recall for a named national report.
xs: **Goa** was the **top state** in the **State of India's Environment 2026 in Figures** — option **(4)**.
The report is by **CSE and Down To Earth**.
**Andhra Pradesh** topped a different index — the **State Energy Efficiency Index 2024**; **Karnataka** topped **SEEI 2023**.
xa: The same report notes **PM2.5 deaths up 61%** in a decade.

**EPI 2026** (Yale and Columbia) ranked India **176th of 177**.

82.s: The Living Planet Report is released by which organisation, and what decline in wildlife was cited for its 2022 edition?
82.x: The Living Planet Report is released by WWF, and its 2022 figure cited a 69% decline in wildlife.
82.tq: Link the publisher with the specific edition and figure.
xs: The **Living Planet Report** is released by **WWF** and cited a **69% wildlife decline** in its **2022** edition — option **(2)**.
It is **biennial**, published **since 1998**.
**61%** is the rise in **PM2.5 deaths** in a decade, from the **State of India's Environment 2026** (CSE and Down To Earth).
xa: ⚠ The **69%** figure is from **LPR 2022**; these notes do not give the LPR 2024 figure.
Other indices: **EPI** = Yale and Columbia; **CCPI** and **CRI** = Germanwatch.
**IUCN** runs the **Red List**: e.g. **Emperor penguin** and **Antarctic fur seal** uplisted to **Endangered** (Apr 2026).

82.s:

82.tq: Track the year carefully when comparing successive editions and leaders.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**SEEI 2024** was prepared by **BEE** (Ministry of Power) with **AEEE**; **Andhra Pradesh** was the **top performer** (asked 2025).
AP's score rose from **83.25** to **87.25** (APSES 2024-25).
**SEEI 2023**: **Karnataka** topped with **86.5**.
xa: ⚠ **SEEI 2024** top = **AP**; **SEEI 2023** top = **Karnataka**.
In **SEEI 2023**, **Assam and UP** were "**Achievers**" (asked 2024).

82.s:
Match the following COPs with their venues:

a. COP28
b. COP29
c. COP30
d. COP31

i. Antalya, Türkiye
ii. Baku, Azerbaijan
iii. Belém, Brazil
iv. Dubai, UAE

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
82.x: COP28 was held in Dubai, COP29 in Baku, COP30 in Belém and COP31 is scheduled for Antalya.
82.tq: Start with the well-known COP28 venue and then place the later venues chronologically.
xs: Correct code: **a–iv, b–ii, c–iii, d–i** — option **(1)**.
**COP28** (2023) → **Dubai, UAE**; **COP29** (2024) → **Baku, Azerbaijan**.
**COP30** (Nov 2025) → **Belém, Brazil**; **COP31** (Nov 2026) → **Antalya, Türkiye**.
xa: **COP32** (2027) → **Addis Ababa, Ethiopia**, the "**Africa COP**".
For **COP33** (2028), **India withdrew its bid** (letter of **2 Apr 2026**).
**COP30** was the **first COP in the Amazon**; at **COP31**, **Australia** presides over negotiations.
⚠ **US$300 bn** NCQG = **COP29 Baku**; **US$1.3 trn** roadmap = **COP30 Belém**.

82.s: Which one of the following was a key outcome of COP28 held in Dubai?
o: The Global Mutirão and 59 adaptation indicators
The first Global Stocktake and a transition away from fossil fuels
A roadmap to US$1.3 trillion per year by 2035
A US$300 billion annual finance commitment by 2035
82.x: COP28 produced the Global Stocktake and called for a transition away from fossil fuels. The other outcomes are associated with COP29 or COP30.
82.tq: Use the COP number and venue to separate outcomes across successive conferences.
xs: **COP28 (Dubai, 2023)** produced the **Global Stocktake** and the call for a **transition away from fossil fuels** — option **(2)**.
**Global Mutirão** and the **59 adaptation indicators** belong to **COP30** (Belém).
The **US$1.3 trn/yr by 2035** Baku-Belém Roadmap is **COP30**; the **US$300 bn** NCQG is **COP29** (Baku).
xa: The **Loss and Damage Fund** was also **operationalised at COP28**.
The **Global River Cities Alliance (GRCA)** was launched at **COP28, Dubai (Dec 2023)**, not New Delhi.
**COP30** also launched Brazil's **TFFF** (US$125 billion forest fund).

82.s: The New Collective Quantified Goal on Climate Finance (NCQG) adopted at COP29 envisaged:
82.x: COP29 at Baku adopted an NCQG of US$300 billion annually by 2035, replacing the earlier US$100 billion commitment.
82.tq: Distinguish the new quantified goal from the earlier finance figure.
xs: The **NCQG** adopted at **COP29 (Baku)** set **US$300 bn per year by 2035** — option **(3)**.
It replaced the earlier **US$100 bn** goal.
**US$1.3 trn/yr by 2035** is the **Baku-Belém Roadmap** of **COP30**.
xa: ⚠ **US$300 bn** = NCQG (COP29); **US$1.3 trn** = Baku-Belém Roadmap (COP30).
**COP30** also agreed to **triple adaptation finance by 2035** and adopted **59 Belém adaptation indicators**.
**COP28 (Dubai)** gave the **Global Stocktake** and operationalised the **Loss and Damage Fund**.

82.s:
Consider the following statements about UNFCCC COP30:
1. It was held at Belem, Brazil, the first COP in the Amazon.
2. It adopted 59 Belem adaptation indicators.
3. It operationalised the Loss and Damage Fund.
4. It set a roadmap to US$1.3 trillion a year in climate finance by 2035.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
82.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct: COP30 (Nov 2025) was at Belem, the first COP in the Amazon, adopted 59 Belem adaptation indicators and set a roadmap to US$1.3 trillion/yr by 2035 (with tripled adaptation finance). Statement 3 is wrong: the Loss and Damage Fund was operationalised at COP28 (Dubai). So '1 and 2 only' is incomplete and the options containing 3 are wrong.
82.tq: Loss and Damage Fund = COP28; US$300 bn NCQG = COP29; US$1.3 trn roadmap = COP30.
xs: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct — option **(2) 1, 2 and 4 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **COP30** (Nov 2025) was at **Belém, Brazil**, the **first COP in the Amazon**.
Statement 2 correct: it adopted **59 Belém adaptation indicators**.
Statement 3 wrong: the **Loss and Damage Fund** was operationalised at **COP28** (Dubai).
Statement 4 correct: the **Baku-Belém Roadmap** aims at **US$1.3 trn/yr by 2035**.
xa: COP30 was called the "**COP of Implementation**"; outcome text: "**Global Mutirão**" / Belém Political Package.
It agreed to **triple adaptation finance by 2035**.
Brazil's **US$125 billion TFFF** was launched at COP30; **India joined as an observer** (2026).

82.s: COP32, scheduled for 2027, is proposed to be held at:
82.x: COP32 is scheduled for 2027 at Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, and is described as the 'Africa COP'.
82.tq: Associate the conference number with its scheduled year and venue.
xs: **COP32** (2027) is to be held at **Addis Ababa, Ethiopia** — option **(3)**, the "**Africa COP**".
**Antalya, Türkiye** hosts **COP31** (2026); **Belém** hosted **COP30**; **Baku** hosted **COP29**.
xa: **COP31** focus: electrification, grids and storage; **Australia** presides over negotiations.
**COP33** (2028): **India withdrew its bid** (letter of **2 Apr 2026**).
"**35 by 35**" (electricity to be **35%** of final energy by 2035) is the **COP31** initiative.

82.s: Which one of the following statements regarding COP33 is correct?
o: India withdrew its bid by a letter dated 2 April 2026.
India was selected to host it in 2028.
India withdrew its bid during COP28 in 2023.
It will be held at Addis Ababa in 2027.
82.x: India withdrew its bid to host COP33, scheduled for 2028, through a letter dated 2 April 2026.
82.tq: Check the distinction between a hosting bid and an awarded venue.
xs: **India withdrew its bid** for **COP33** (2028) by a **letter of 2 Apr 2026** — option **(1)** (TH, 9 Apr 2026).
So India was **not selected** to host it, and the withdrawal was in **2026**, not at **COP28**.
**Addis Ababa** hosts **COP32** in **2027**, not COP33.
xa: **COP31** (Nov 2026): **Antalya, Türkiye**, with **Australia** presiding over negotiations.
**COP30** (Nov 2025): **Belém, Brazil**, the first COP in the Amazon.
**BASIC** group: **Brazil, South Africa, India, China**.

82.s:
Consider the following statements:

2. The Loss and Damage Fund was operationalised at COP29 in Baku.
3. Bhutan, Suriname and Panama are carbon-negative countries.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
82.x: Statement 1 is correct: BASIC = Brazil, South Africa, India, China. Statement 2 is wrong: the Loss and Damage Fund was operationalised at COP28 (Dubai); COP29 at Baku is known for the US$300 bn NCQG. Statement 3 is correct: Bhutan, Suriname and Panama are carbon-negative. So '1 only' is incomplete and options with 2 are wrong.
82.tq: Loss and Damage Fund operationalised at COP28, Dubai.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(3) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **BASIC** = **Brazil, South Africa, India and China**.
Statement 2 wrong: the **Loss and Damage Fund** was operationalised at **COP28 (Dubai)**; **COP29 Baku** is known for the **US$300 bn NCQG**.
Statement 3 correct: **Bhutan, Suriname and Panama** are **carbon-negative** countries.
xa: **COP28** also gave the **Global Stocktake** and the call to **transition away from fossil fuels**.
India's long-term goal is **net zero by 2070**.
⚠ **US$300 bn** = NCQG (COP29); **US$1.3 trn** = Baku-Belém Roadmap (COP30).

82.s: CITES CoP20, held in 2025, was hosted by which city and country?
82.x: CITES CoP20 was held at Samarkand in Uzbekistan, marking the first CITES CoP in Central Asia.
82.tq: Distinguish the CITES venue from the venues of the other environmental COPs.
xs: **CITES CoP20** (2025) was held at **Samarkand, Uzbekistan**, the **first in Central Asia** — option **(4)**.
**Victoria Falls, Zimbabwe** hosted **Ramsar COP15**; **Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia** hosted **UNCCD COP17**; **Belém** hosted **UNFCCC COP30**.
xa: CoP20 added **77 species**; **whale shark, oceanic whitetip and manta rays** went to **Appendix I**.
**India blocked the EU bid** to list **Guggul**.

82.s: Which of the following groups of species was moved to Appendix I at CITES CoP20?
o: Whale shark, oceanic whitetip shark and manta rays
Guggul, whale shark and snow leopard
Olive Ridley turtle, whale and dugong
82.x: Whale shark, oceanic whitetip shark and manta rays were included in Appendix I at CITES CoP20.
82.tq: Test the exact species grouping instead of relying on a general wildlife association.
xs: **Whale shark, oceanic whitetip and manta rays** were moved to **Appendix I** at **CITES CoP20** — option **(1)**.
**Guggul** was not listed: **India blocked the EU bid** to list it.
xa: CoP20 was held at **Samarkand, Uzbekistan** (2025), the **first in Central Asia**.
In all, **77 species** were added at CoP20.
**Olive Ridley** turtles are protected in India by the Coast Guard's **Operation Olivia**, using **Turtle Excluder Devices**.

82.s: Which proposal was blocked by India at CITES CoP20?
o: The proposal of Brazil to list manta rays in Appendix I
The European Union bid to list Guggul
The Ramsar proposal concerning wetland cities
The proposal of Mongolia to list steppe species
82.x: India blocked the European Union’s bid to list Guggul at CITES CoP20.
82.tq: Apply the ‘who blocked what’ trap to identify the correct proposal and country grouping.
xs: India **blocked the European Union's bid to list Guggul** at **CITES CoP20** — option **(2)**.
**Manta rays** were in fact moved to **Appendix I**, along with the **whale shark** and **oceanic whitetip**.
xa: CITES CoP20 (2025) met at **Samarkand, Uzbekistan**, the **first in Central Asia**.
It added **77 species** to the CITES lists.
⚠ Other COPs: **Ramsar COP15** = Victoria Falls; **CMS COP15** = Campo Grande; **UNCCD COP17** = Ulaanbaatar.

82.s: The Victoria Falls Declaration and the 5th Strategic Plan for 2025–30 are associated with which meeting?
82.x: Ramsar COP15, held at Victoria Falls in Zimbabwe, produced the Victoria Falls Declaration and the 5th Strategic Plan for 2025–30.
82.tq: Start from the distinctive decision and identify the correct convention meeting.
xs: The **Victoria Falls Declaration** and the **5th Strategic Plan 2025-30** came from **Ramsar COP15** (Jul 2025, **Victoria Falls, Zimbabwe**) — option **(1)**.
**CMS COP15** was at **Campo Grande, Brazil**; **UNCCD COP17** at **Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia**; **UNFCCC COP30** at **Belém**.
xa: At Ramsar COP15, **Jayshree Vencatesan** became the **first Indian** to win the **Ramsar Award**.
The **Ramsar Convention** dates from **1971**; India joined in **1982**.
India's **101st** Ramsar site is **Glaw Lake (Arunachal)**, 3 Aug 2026.
⚠ **COP15** twice: **Ramsar** = Victoria Falls; **CMS** = Campo Grande.

82.s: Who became the first Indian to win the Ramsar Award?
82.x: Jayshree Vencatesan became the first Indian to win the Ramsar Award.
82.tq: Use the first-person distinction in a current-affairs award question.
xs: **Jayshree Vencatesan** became the **first Indian** to win the **Ramsar Award** — option **(2)**, at **Ramsar COP15** (Victoria Falls, Jul 2025).
**Hamataliwa papikonda** is not a person: it is a new **lynx spider** found in **Papikonda NP, AP**.
xa: Ramsar COP15 adopted the **Victoria Falls Declaration** and the **5th Strategic Plan 2025-30**.
India: **1st in Asia, 3rd in the world** in Ramsar sites, after **UK (176)** and **Mexico (144)**.
**Tamil Nadu** has the most Ramsar sites (**20**); **Indore** was India's first **Wetland City**.

82.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. CMS COP15 — Campo Grande, Brazil
2. UNCCD COP17 — Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia
3. Ramsar COP15 — Samarkand, Uzbekistan
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
82.x: CMS COP15 was held at Campo Grande, Brazil, and UNCCD COP17 at Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia. Ramsar COP15 was held at Victoria Falls, Zimbabwe, not Samarkand.
82.tq: Find the incorrectly matched venue before choosing the coded combination.

82.s:
Consider the following statements about India's updated Nationally Determined Contribution announced in March 2026:
1. It targets 60% non-fossil installed power capacity by 2035.
2. It targets a 47% reduction in emission intensity of GDP from the 2005 level.
3. It specifies a carbon sink of 3.5–4 billion tonnes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
82.x: The updated NDC sets all three targets: 60% non-fossil capacity, a 47% reduction in GDP emission intensity from 2005, and a 3.5–4 billion-tonne carbon sink.
82.tq: Keep the revised NDC figures separate from the earlier 2022 targets.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Non-fossil power capacity**: **60%** by **2035**.
**Emission intensity** of GDP: a **47%** cut from **2005** levels by 2035.
**Extra carbon sink**: **3.5-4 bn tonnes** CO2e.
xa: The updated NDC (for **2031-35**) was approved by the **Cabinet on 25 Mar 2026**.
The **2022 NDC** (2030) targets: **50%** non-fossil (achieved in **2025**), **44%** intensity cut, **2.5-3 bn t** sink.
Long-term goal: **net zero by 2070**.

xs: Statements 2 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 2 and 3 only**.

Statement 2 correct: **50% non-fossil** installed power capacity by **2030**.
Statement 3 correct: the **50%** target was **achieved in 2025**.
xa: ⚠ The notes give the 2030 intensity target as **45%** in one line and **44%** in the 2022 NDC line.
Updated NDC (by **2035**): **60%** non-fossil, **47%** intensity cut, **3.5-4 bn t** sink.
The 2022 NDC's carbon sink target was **2.5-3 bn t**.

96.s:
Consider the following statements about the Padma awards:
1. The Padma Vibhushan is given for exceptional and distinguished service and is India's second-highest civilian award.
2. The Padma Bhushan is given for distinguished service in any field and is India's fourth-highest civilian award.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
96.x: Statement 1 is correct: Padma Vibhushan = exceptional and distinguished service, 2nd highest. Statement 2 is wrong: Padma Bhushan is for distinguished service of a high order and is 3rd highest; 'distinguished service in any field' and 4th place describe the Padma Shri. So only 1 is correct; 2 only, both and neither are wrong.
96.tq: Vibhushan = exceptional (2nd), Bhushan = high order (3rd), Shri = any field (4th).
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1 correct: the **Padma Vibhushan** is for **exceptional and distinguished service** and is the **2nd highest** civilian award.
Statement 2 wrong: the **Padma Bhushan** is for **distinguished service of high order** and ranks **3rd**; "any field" and **4th** describe the **Padma Shri**.
xa: The **Bharat Ratna** was last given in **2024** (**5** awardees, incl. **P.V. Narasimha Rao**).
Padma awards were instituted in **1954**; announced on **Republic Day**.

96.s:
Consider the following statements about the Padma awards:
1. They were instituted in 1954.
2. They are announced every year on Independence Day.
3. They are conferred by the President at Rashtrapati Bhavan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
96.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Padma awards were instituted in 1954. Statement 2 is wrong: they are announced on Republic Day, not Independence Day. Statement 3 is correct: the President confers them at Rashtrapati Bhavan (around March-April). Hence 1 and 3 only; any option containing 2 is wrong, and '1 only' misses statement 3.
96.tq: Padma = Republic Day announcement, President confers, since 1954.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(4) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 correct: the Padma awards were **instituted in 1954**.
Statement 2 wrong: they are announced on **Republic Day**, not Independence Day.
Statement 3 correct: the **President** confers them at **Rashtrapati Bhavan** (around March-April).
xa: ⚠ **1954** = Padma awards instituted + **Sahitya Akademi** inaugurated.
2026 awards were presented in **two investitures**, the second at **Ganatantra Mandap**, Rashtrapati Bhavan.
Legal status: **not "titles" under Art. 18** (**Balaji Raghavan case, 1996**).

96.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the constitutional status of the Padma awards:
1. They are not titles prohibited by Article 18 of the Constitution.
2. Article 18 expressly bars military and academic distinctions.
3. They may be used as prefixes or suffixes to a recipient’s name.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
96.x: Only statement 1 is correct: the Balaji Raghavan case (1996) held that Padma awards are not 'titles' under Article 18. Statement 2 is wrong: Article 18 exempts military and academic distinctions rather than barring them. Statement 3 is wrong: the awards cannot be used as prefixes or suffixes. So 1 only.
96.tq: Watch for the reversed constitutional exception and the false claim about use as a title.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1 correct: the **Balaji Raghavan case (1996)** held that Padma awards are **not "titles" under Art. 18**.
Statement 2 wrong: **Art. 18** **exempts** military and academic distinctions; it does not bar them.
Statement 3 wrong: the awards **cannot be used as prefix or suffix**.
xa: The same rule applies to the **Bharat Ratna**.
**Padma Vibhushan** is the **2nd highest** civilian award; **Padma Bhushan** 3rd; **Padma Shri** 4th.
AP demanded the Bharat Ratna for **NTR** (Feb 2026).

96.s: In which case was it held that national civilian awards such as the Padma awards are not titles under Article 18?
96.x: The Balaji Raghavan case of 1996 dealt with the status of national awards under Article 18.
96.tq: Match the constitutional issue with the case specifically associated with it.
xs: The **Balaji Raghavan case (1996)** held that national awards are **not "titles" under Art. 18** — option **(4)**.
Hence they cannot be used as a **prefix or suffix** to the name.
xa: **Art. 18** exempts **military and academic distinctions**.
The ruling covers both the **Padma awards** and the **Bharat Ratna**.
**Bharat Ratna** last given in **2024** to **5** awardees.

103.s: R. Rithika Sri is associated with which distinction?

India's first cricketer to play 200 T20Is

o: Ferran Torres — scorer in the final

**Mbappé** = **Golden Boot** (10 goals) and **Ferran Torres** scored the winner in the final — both correct.
xa: ⚠ **Mbappé** = Golden Boot + all-time WC top scorer (**22**); **Rodri** = Golden Ball.
**Spain** beat **Argentina 1-0** aet at **MetLife Stadium** (USA), **19 Jul 2026**.

Spain beat **Argentina 1-0** aet at **MetLife Stadium**.

Statement 3 is correct: it was the first in India since **2002 (Hyderabad)**.
xa: Sindarov also won **Candidates 2026** (Pegeia, Cyprus) and plays **D. Gukesh** in **Geneva**.

115.s:

115.tq: UNSG term = 5 years; UNSC recommends, UNGA appoints.
xs: Only statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **António Guterres** leaves at the **end of 2026**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the term is **5 years**, not six; the successor's term starts **1 Jan 2027**.
Statement 3 is correct: under **Art. 97**, the **UNGA appoints on UNSC recommendation**.
xa: The UNSC held its **first straw poll** in **Aug 2026**.
Straw poll rule: at least **9 "Encourage"** votes out of **15** + **no P5 "Discourage"** vote.

115.tq: Break a procedural rule into its numerical threshold and veto-related condition.
xs: A candidate needs at least **9 "Encourage"** votes out of **15** and **no P5 "Discourage"** vote — so option **(1)** is correct.
Unanimity, a 10-vote rule ignoring the P5, or a prior UNGA vote are not part of the rule.
xa: The **first straw poll** was held in **Aug 2026**, as **Guterres** leaves at the end of 2026.
The Secretary-General has a **5-year** term; appointment under **Art. 97** (UNGA on UNSC recommendation).
